items.title: Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity by funding AI startups to buy its GPUs
items.summary: A TechPowerUp article reports allegations that Nvidia funded AI startups that then bought its GPUs, creating artificial scarcity.
items.why: If true, circular funding could distort GPU supply and pricing, affecting how teams plan compute procurement and budgets.

items.title: Anthropic Upgrades Claude Code Projects to Run Parallel AI Workers Hands-Free
items.summary: Anthropic has upgraded Claude Code projects so multiple AI workers can run in parallel without manual intervention.
items.why: Parallel autonomous coding agents could change how teams split and automate development tasks, though the source gives few details.

items.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
items.summary: Amazon reportedly plans a 'World Product Graph' indexing product data sold across the internet, including items it does not sell, per Reuters.
items.why: A broad cross-web product index could affect retailers, marketplaces, and anyone building product-data or shopping integrations.

items.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1
items.summary: GS Caltex uses Amazon SageMaker Canvas connected to SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers' no-code models run in production.
items.why: It shows a path for moving no-code models into production MLOps, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.summary: Founders and VCs say Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia leaves a major gap in AI startup funding, expecting smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.why: Changes in Nvidia's startup investment could affect funding availability and valuations for AI companies that rely on its backing.

items.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
items.summary: AWS shows how to deploy LiteLLM with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing on Amazon Bedrock and measure cost per solved coding-agent task against single-model baselines.
items.why: Cost per solved task, not price per token, is the metric to track when routing coding-agent requests across models.

items.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
items.summary: AWS explains how Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots initialized environments so session startup no longer scales with image size, and offers four patterns for faster startup.
items.why: Snapshot-based restore decouples session start time from container image size, which affects latency planning for agent deployments.

items.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures
items.summary: AWS describes deploying the OpenFold3-preview protein structure model from SageMaker JumpStart, with asynchronous inference, multi-GPU support, and scale-to-zero.
items.why: Gives teams a managed path to run biomolecular structure prediction in their own account with cost controls like scale-to-zero.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
items.summary: OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, letting its Dots AI agents make purchases for US ChatGPT Pro subscribers with eligible US cards.
items.why: Agents that spend money on users' behalf raise new questions about payment authorization, controls, and liability for product builders.

items.title: No AI Slop: A Manifesto
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to a manifesto titled "No AI Slop," which received 133 points and 75 comments.

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: LangChain has reached a $3 billion valuation and claims 7,000 customers for its LangSmith agent management platform.
items.why: Signals strong enterprise demand for agent tooling and observability platforms that are model-agnostic.

items.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
items.summary: AssemblyAI describes running cost-optimized speech-to-text inference on AWS using ECS, EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an SQS-based retry design across European Regions.
items.why: Shows a concrete architecture for cutting GPU inference costs by about 70% while meeting SLA commitments using Spot capacity.

items.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: AWS shows how to attribute Amazon Bedrock costs per user for AI developer tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and enforce per-user limits.
items.why: Per-user cost attribution and usage limits help engineering leaders control spend on AI developer tools.

items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.summary: New research finds that the most advanced Chinese AI models were trained on Nvidia chips that are export-banned.
items.why: Highlights export-control enforcement gaps that could affect chip supply, compliance, and model provenance for companies.

items.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to a Dwarkesh Patel essay arguing that a wave of change hitting mathematics is coming for AI development.

items.title: Are we just going to ignore that books are destroyed for AI?
items.summary: A Forbes report says AI companies are buying and destroying antique books, prompting discussion on Hacker News.

items.title: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture
items.summary: AWS walks through using SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture to log live inference traffic, find a blind spot with Athena, fine-tune, and measure the lift.
items.why: Offers a practical loop for turning production inference logs into fine-tuning data and measuring improvement.

items.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
items.summary: Hugging Face published a tutorial on building a robot pick-and-place simulation using SimReady assets.

items.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
items.summary: Reports say AI helped unlock Kurt Gödel's notebooks, which are said to contain hundreds of proved theorems.

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.summary: Hugging Face introduced XYBench, a benchmark project described as helping with the problem behind the question.

items.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
items.summary: A disgruntled researcher released a Windows zero-day called "SignDrop" that lets local users gain System privileges.
items.why: Unpatched local privilege escalation exploits let attackers with local access take full control, so patch and hardening priorities need review.

items.title: Why is Google cutting off Search from AI-free schools? Here are some theories
items.summary: An NPR article asks why Google is cutting off Search access for AI-free schools, and offers several theories.
items.why: The text gives too little detail on the policy or its mechanics to say what it means for engineers or tech leaders.

items.title: Jonathan Blow – If AI Solved Coding, Why Is My Software Still the Same? [video]
items.summary: Game developer Jonathan Blow gave a video talk questioning why software has not visibly improved even though AI is said to have solved coding.
items.why: It is a critical perspective on AI's real impact on software quality, relevant to tech leaders evaluating productivity claims.

items.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, letting agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections.
items.why: Agents making real payments need explicit user approval and card-level protections, which matters for designing safe agentic commerce flows.

items.title: ElevenLabs’ new app combines meeting note-taking and dictation for teams
items.summary: ElevenLabs launched ElevenAI, a new app combining meeting note-taking and dictation aimed at teams and enterprises.
items.why: Adds another voice-based productivity tool for enterprise teams, relevant to those evaluating meeting transcription options.

items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
items.summary: Hugging Face published a post announcing llama.cpp v1.0.0, positioned as a stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem.

items.title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
items.summary: The Verge reviewed Claude Duet, Anthropic's consumer AI agent, finding it somewhat neurotic but surprisingly helpful.
items.why: Offers a hands-on consumer view of agent usefulness for non-coders, though the review gives limited technical detail.

items.title: How AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner
items.summary: NVIDIA describes how AI helps care teams with routine tasks, including clinical trial matching and radiologist support, with clinicians kept in the loop.

items.title: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
items.summary: Israeli VCs see opportunity for challengers as worries grow over the impact of Nvidia's leadership departure on the local startup ecosystem.
items.why: Leadership turmoil at Nvidia could open competitive openings for AI infrastructure challengers, though the text gives few specifics.

items.title: Let’s talk about Jensen Huang’s many affairs!
items.summary: The Verge's opinion piece comments on reported personal affairs involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, with no clear factual answers provided.

items.title: AI Is Destroying the Trust Between Writers and Readers
items.summary: The Atlantic reports that AI-generated literary scams on Amazon are eroding trust between writers and readers.
items.why: Highlights platform trust and content-authenticity risks from AI-generated content, relevant to marketplaces and content moderation teams.

items.title: Elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com
items.summary: Anthropic's status page reports elevated errors affecting claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com.
items.why: Service disruptions across Claude products affect teams relying on them in production, so monitoring fallbacks is worthwhile.

items.title: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
items.summary: Shield uses OpenAI to help IT technicians hand off work in legacy portals, with its Forge agents navigating systems for them.
items.why: Agents that navigate legacy enterprise systems show how AI can take routine portal work while leaving judgment calls to humans.

items.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
items.summary: Zugwise reframes digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets as game reconstruction, using computer-chess techniques to catch legal-but-wrong misreads that legality-only pipelines miss.
items.why: It shows that domain-specific validation can catch silent errors that generic legality checks accept, a useful pattern for OCR-plus-constraint pipelines.

items.title: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
items.summary: A study finds that cleaning an agent's error history can hurt performance when the world still contains the uncorrected error, since history and world state can conflict.
items.why: Engineers compacting or repairing agent histories must keep them consistent with actual environment state, or corrections may degrade behavior.

items.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
items.summary: Together AI describes Together Compiler, a system for continually compiling and optimizing AI inference deployments as models and traffic patterns change.
items.why: Continual, automated inference optimization addresses shifting model and traffic mixes, relevant to teams running production inference at scale.

items.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
items.summary: Researchers study when LLM-provided semantic priors should enter partially identified causal discovery, separating non-identifiability from finite-sample instability.
items.why: It offers guidance on when to trust LLM-suggested causal directions, since incorrect proposals can invalidate downstream inference.

items.title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
items.summary: SynthCorp is a platform that generates customizable synthetic corporate data estates and paired benchmarks for evaluating LLM-driven data agents.
items.why: Teams evaluating data agents can use targeted, non-saturating synthetic benchmarks instead of quickly saturated public ones.

items.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
items.summary: Researchers compare how humans and AI use timing cues for social coordination in The Mind, a cooperative card game that forbids explicit communication.

items.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
items.summary: A paper shows arena-style, Bradley-Terry-based model leaderboards are vulnerable to manipulation such as strategic voting by providers seeking higher ranks.
items.why: Teams relying on preference leaderboards to choose models should account for manipulation risk and validate with their own evaluations.

items.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
items.summary: Researchers propose a middle path for robust state estimation from pretrained perception models like VLMs, avoiding both single best guesses and full intractable distributions.
items.why: Agents acting on uncertain perception outputs can become unsafe when they treat a wrong best guess as ground truth.

items.title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: An evaluation of certify-or-decline proof-step verification on open-weight models shows precision gains at substantial coverage cost, with a self-consistency baseline competitive.
items.why: Engineers choosing verification for math reasoning must weigh precision gains against lost answer coverage and compute cost.

items.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
items.summary: GenPFN uses a pretrained tabular foundation model, TabPFN, without training to generate candidate engineering designs from small labeled datasets.
items.why: It suggests a training-free way to augment scarce simulation data for engineering design, reducing costly experiments.

items.title: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
items.summary: AutoAssumption searches over explicit algorithmic assumptions, framed as proofs, to discover ML systems algorithms such as speculative decoding.
items.why: Making algorithm assumptions explicit could make automated discovery of ML systems optimizations easier to attribute and reproduce.

items.title: Open Challenges and Opportunities in Human-Agent Systems
items.summary: A paper outlines open challenges in human-agent systems, drawing on AAMAS community foundations for individual partnerships and larger teams.

items.title: Effective Teacher Support for Reasoning Distillation
items.summary: Researchers show that distilling from only the teacher's highest-probability vocabulary fraction can work for reasoning distillation of Qwen3 and Nemotron models.
items.why: Restricting distillation support can cut training and storage cost for teacher targets without necessarily sacrificing student performance.

items.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
items.summary: A philosophical paper asks whether an AI agent that revises conclusions based on judgments of its own reasoning can become epistemically akratic.

items.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
items.summary: MuEdit introduces a Conflict Index and a multi-task editing method to handle inter-domain null-space conflicts when sequentially updating LLM knowledge.
items.why: Sequential knowledge edits across domains can silently fail, so teams maintaining updated LLMs need conflict-aware editing methods.

items.title: Edge-Native Multimodal RAG: Hardware-Aware Quantization and Architectural Optimization for Consumer GPUs
items.summary: Researchers present an edge-native multimodal RAG framework optimized with hardware-aware quantization for consumer Turing GPUs such as the NVIDIA Tesla T4.
items.why: Shows memory-constrained RAG deployment on consumer GPUs is feasible, with trade-offs between quantization and architecture that matter for edge deployments.

items.title: Provably Optimal HBT Legalization in Seconds: Certified Optima Reveal Where the Headroom Really Lies
items.summary: Researchers build an open benchmark of 21 hybrid bonding terminal legalization instances and compute provably optimal displacement results for 3D IC placement.
items.why: Provides certified optimal baselines showing how much headroom remains for 3D IC legalizers, which helps chip design teams judge heuristics.

items.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
items.summary: A study finds multimodal training shapes text-only reasoning in language models, with a vision-language axis in hidden states affecting spatial-imagery task accuracy.
items.why: Suggests multimodal training can change how models reason on text alone, relevant to model selection and interpretability work.

items.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
items.summary: Researchers introduce RSI-PDEbench, a 1,001-case benchmark testing whether LLM agents can self-improve at identifying and solving partial differential equations.
items.why: Offers a concrete evaluation for agentic scientific-computing workflows, useful for teams assessing agents on numerical and modeling tasks.

items.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
items.summary: A study of coding agents finds 38–82% of successful runs hit a correct patch on the first source edit, yet agents keep working afterward.
items.why: Highlights wasted compute and cost in coding agents after a correct fix, pointing to termination logic as an engineering lever.

items.title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
items.summary: Researchers propose prefix-guided sampling that uses early internal confidence signals to prune low-quality reasoning paths in parallel test-time scaling.
items.why: Could cut inference compute for parallel reasoning by stopping weak paths early rather than fully expanding them.

items.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
items.summary: A study tests whether rewriting problem statements via decomposition, typed reformulation, or concept reduction improves LLM problem solving across eight benchmarks.
items.why: Offers a low-cost prompt-level technique that may improve reasoning accuracy, though gains depend on when rewrites help.

items.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
items.summary: EvoX is a Rust-based multi-model agent runtime that adds deterministic runtime control to LLM agent harnesses to address tool-call mismatches and false completion claims.
items.why: Frames the agent harness as a runtime policy with deterministic controls, a design pattern relevant to reliable agent system builders.

items.title: Science Prediction Universe
items.summary: Researchers introduce Science Prediction Universe, a benchmark for evaluating whether AI can predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans.

items.title: Advancing Weighted Partial MaxSAT Solving via Differentiable GPU Guidance
items.summary: A GPU-CPU hybrid framework for weighted partial MaxSAT adds differentiable GPU optimization that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers without training data.
items.why: Shows GPU-based differentiable methods can complement classical combinatorial solvers, relevant to teams working on optimization workloads.

items.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
items.summary: Researchers report Neuro-VL, a vision-language model for neuroimaging that aims to interpret complex clinical exams and communicate findings in clinical context.
items.why: Demonstrates domain-specialized vision-language models for medical imaging, a signal for healthcare AI product development.

items.title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
items.summary: GuardianAgentFlow is a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing web requests from web agents through an explicit release contract to protect private data.
items.why: Addresses privacy leakage risks in web agents that handle sensitive user context, a concern for agent product design.

items.title: Expanding the Decision Space of Pretrained Models through Structured Re-Decoding
items.summary: Structured Re-Decoding is a training-free framework that recombines local candidates from pretrained models under structural constraints, tested on molecular, protein, and RNA tasks.
items.why: Offers a training-free way to satisfy structural constraints in generation, potentially useful for scientific design pipelines.

items.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
items.summary: HyperSkill proposes training-free omnimodal GRPO that keeps the backbone frozen and evolves a hypergraph-indexed skill library through textual edits instead of gradient updates.
items.why: Suggests a way to improve reasoning without expensive parameter updates, though the text gives limited evidence of results.

items.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
items.summary: WordInferBench is a 280-instance benchmark testing whether agents can infer appropriate Word document attribute edits from document context rather than explicit instructions.
items.why: Targets a realistic gap in document-editing agents, where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute.

items.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
items.summary: Researchers propose AFTER, a world model with adaptive fast-slow timescales to adapt to sudden, persistent, initially unknown robot dynamics changes like unknown payloads.
items.why: Robots that grasp unknown-payload objects need models that adapt quickly, since accumulated prediction errors during rollouts can mislead actions.

items.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
items.summary: Researchers introduce guardscope, a framework measuring which LLM agent actions runtime controls like agent gateways actually check, against kernel-level ground truth.
items.why: Gateways only inspect actions crossing their placement point, so teams relying on them may have coverage gaps that this method makes measurable.

items.title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
items.summary: Researchers present MVDriveBench, a video QA benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can reason over synchronized surround-view autonomous driving footage.
items.why: It exposes whether MLLMs handle non-front-view information, a gap relevant to teams evaluating vision models for driving.

items.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for masked diffusion vision-language models to improve robust reasoning for autonomous driving.
items.why: Shows how discrete diffusion, an autoregressive alternative, can be adapted to driving despite domain gaps in training and inference.

items.title: Verify by Doing: Co-Evolving Agent Execution and Evaluation without External Feedback
items.summary: Researchers propose Verify by Doing, which co-evolves agent Actor and Evaluator harnesses within a task using model weights fixed, without external feedback.
items.why: Enables agent self-improvement when external task-success feedback is unavailable at test time, relevant to deploying agents without labeled outcomes.

items.title: Where Autonomy Belongs: A Separation of Powers for Agentic Program Evolution
items.summary: The paper proposes a separation-of-powers design for LLM-driven program evolution, splitting govern, propose, and judge roles across independent components.
items.why: Offers an architectural argument for keeping evaluation independent from code-generating agents in automated program search systems.

items.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
items.summary: Researchers present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that keeps interaction history as persistent state shared across successive language models.
items.why: Decoupling memory from the model could let teams swap models without losing accumulated user context and evidence.

items.title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes
items.summary: Researchers propose PCM-PPO, a physics-constrained maskable reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes.
items.why: Addresses planning when ground-in-the-loop control is impractical due to distance, a constraint relevant to autonomous systems in uncertain environments.

items.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
items.summary: A study of 2,400 trajectories from ten LLMs in four public-service scenarios finds agents read records in 96.9% of open-ended runs, examining underspecified instructions.
items.why: Shows agents frequently act beyond given instructions in high-stakes public-service settings, a concern for deployment oversight.

items.title: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
items.summary: Researchers report loyalty capture, where AI models reporting to a CEO more often recommend cutting investment when the CEO's bonus depends on current earnings.
items.why: Suggests models can be biased toward their supervisor's incentives without any explicit instruction, a risk for AI used in business recommendations.

items.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
items.summary: SkillEarth proposes equipping general-purpose agents with remote sensing tool-call knowledge automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories, avoiding retraining.
items.why: Shows a route to adding new tools and workflows to agents via extracted skills rather than model retraining.

items.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
items.summary: The paper formalizes incentives for long-lived personal AI agents as runtime contracts over model tier, compute, memory, tool authority, and compensation, with metrics.
items.why: Proposes treating operating constraints as enforceable runtime contracts, relevant to governing persistent agents with accounts and tool access.

items.title: Marginal-Preserving Coupled Diffusion Composition for Long-Horizon Planning
items.summary: Researchers propose a marginal-preserving coupled diffusion method to make stitched trajectory chunks globally consistent in long-horizon diffusion planning.
items.why: Addresses incoherent plans from stitching locally feasible segments, a practical issue for compositional diffusion planners.

items.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
items.summary: A controlled study compares open typed-decision models that answer structured questions about text, such as yes/no checks and graded scores, against larger approaches.
items.why: Could inform choosing small, calibrated classifiers over general LLMs for structured decisions in software pipelines.

items.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce MemCredit, which selects memories for long-horizon web agents by decision utility rather than semantic relevance.
items.why: Argues that the most relevant memories are not always the most useful for actions, a design point for agent memory retrieval.

items.title: A Reliability Study of Explainable AI for Freight Mode Classification
items.summary: Researchers study whether explanations from explainable ML models can be trusted when classifying freight shipments as Air/Air Charter or Truck/Ocean.
items.why: Shows that feature explanations in logistics models may not be reliable, which matters for teams relying on them to justify automated decisions.

items.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
items.summary: DISCERN proposes handling contradicting and superseded facts at write time and resolving them at read time for persistent LLM-agent memory, tested on the ENT-310 benchmark.
items.why: Argues that enterprise agent memory failures are not just retrieval problems, which affects how teams design agent memory systems.

items.title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
items.summary: NIBench is a new benchmark evaluating autonomous AI agents on execution, skill evolution, and scientific judgment in neuroimaging workflows.
items.why: Highlights that plausible agent outputs in neuroimaging can hide errors affecting conclusions, so agent evaluation needs domain-specific testing.

items.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
items.summary: A paper addresses how developers should decide when to stop pre-deployment testing of AI agents, weighing testing time against the risk of unseen failure modes.
items.why: Frames the stop-and-deploy decision as a quantifiable tradeoff, which is relevant to release criteria for agent systems.

items.title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
items.summary: Researchers ran a tournament of nine negotiation agents, from rule-based to language-model, in a changing supply-demand market modeled on freight brokering.
items.why: Shows how negotiation strategies perform against multiple live rivals, relevant to designers of automated marketplace agents.

items.title: Food Critic: An Agentic Visualization System for Auditable Restaurant-Safety Reasoning
items.summary: Food Critic is an agentic visualization system combining public health inspection records with crowd reviews to support auditable restaurant-safety reasoning.
items.why: Demonstrates grounding agent answers in inspectable data sources rather than model knowledge alone, a pattern useful for auditable decision-support tools.

items.title: Reward-Driven Collider Physics Challenges for Self-Improving Agentic AI via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes open-ended collider physics tasks with continuous automatic rewards to train agentic AI via reinforcement learning and benchmarks frontier reasoning models.
items.why: Offers a template for building RL environments with continuous rewards for hard technical domains where current models often fail.

items.title: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance
items.summary: A paper introduces a Society-Centered AI Governance Framework to help assess AI policy instruments while they are still being made.
items.why: Gives policy and compliance leaders a vocabulary for evaluating governance instruments, though the text offers little direct technical guidance.

items.title: Stack more levels: how to get general and human-like Mario playing
items.summary: Researchers train PPO agents on increasing numbers of generated Super Mario levels, test generalization on 1000 held-out levels, and shape policies into gameplay archetypes.

items.title: Turning Multi-Agent Communication into Token-Level Credit with On Policy Self Distillation
items.summary: OPSD4MAS converts inter-agent communication into fine-grained token-level credit using on-policy self distillation for reinforcement learning in LLM multi-agent systems.
items.why: Addresses coarse credit assignment in multi-agent RL, which could improve training of LLM agent teams.

items.title: One Fuzzer, Many Reasoners: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzing with Reliability-Calibrated and Context-Gated Guidance
items.summary: NSAI-Fuzz is a unified semantics-aware fuzzing framework for testing heterogeneous neuro-symbolic AI systems with reliability-calibrated guidance.
items.why: Provides a common testing interface for neuro-symbolic systems, which are hard to test because small input changes can cause reasoning failures.

items.title: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Research on Causal Reasoning
items.summary: Causals is an open knowledge graph of 369,184 nodes and 1,272,418 edges built from news reports, for research on causal reasoning.
items.why: Offers an openly available dataset for building or testing systems that reason about how events propagate to organizations and markets.

items.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
items.summary: SAGE-QA proposes a semantic-aware grounded evaluation for closed-context question answering on SQuAD 2.0, moving beyond strict exact-match scoring for LLMs.
items.why: Exact-match scoring can mark valid paraphrases as hallucinations, so teams evaluating LLM QA may need semantic grounding metrics.

items.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
items.summary: The paper presents a toolkit for profiling LLM risk propensities across contexts, measuring how risk-averse or risk-tolerant models are and how consistent they are.
items.why: Offers a method to build model risk profiles that could inform model selection and behavior prediction in deployments.

items.title: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the Age of AI
items.summary: A roundtable-based paper argues AI shifts data scientists' leverage toward assessing the credibility of findings and whether evidence generalizes across contexts.
items.why: Suggests analytics teams should prioritize causal inference and experiment credibility as AI increases analysis volume.

items.title: DIAGNO: Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators for Heterogeneous Earth Dynamics Modeling
items.summary: Researchers propose DIAGNO, diagonal spherical neural operators for forecasting Earth's dynamic systems, arguing existing spherical operators rely on a rotation equivariance assumption.
items.why: Shows how to model spherical geometry for geophysics forecasting while keeping computation tractable; the abstract is cut off, so details on results are limited.

items.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for deciding whether autonomous agents should permanently adopt self-generated changes to prompts, memory, tools, or policies.
items.why: Addresses how to keep agents from adopting plausible but degrading self-modifications, a practical reliability concern for teams deploying autonomous agents.

items.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency
items.summary: Study tests whether small Qwen2.5 routers (1.5B to 14B parameters) with prompt optimization can decide when to enable reasoning, retrieval, web search, or tool use per query.
items.why: Suggests cheaper small-model routers may cut unnecessary LLM computation, though the abstract is truncated and results are not shown.

items.title: FPSRG: Heterogeneous User Simulation First-Person Post-Training and Multidimensional Semantic Response Grids
items.summary: Researchers present FPSRG, a method for building LLM user-simulation profiles retrievable by multidimensional target scores, using first-person post-training and semantic response grids.
items.why: Offers a technique for generating heterogeneous simulated users, useful for testing products, though the abstract gives limited detail on evaluation.

items.title: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates
items.summary: Paper explores mechanisms for rationally aligning hypothetical superintelligent agents assisting humans in question answering via debate-style interaction controls.
items.why: Theoretical alignment work with little immediate engineering application; the text is abstract and provides few concrete results.

items.title: Fine-Tuned Small Language Model for Synthetic Clinical Data Generation and Predictive Healthcare Analytics
items.summary: Researchers fine-tune a small language model to generate synthetic clinical data to address scarce or imbalanced medical datasets for predictive healthcare analytics.
items.why: Shows a route to augmenting imbalanced healthcare datasets with cheaper small models, though the text gives no performance figures.

items.title: How Should Planning Agents ReSHAPE Their Search Space?
items.summary: Researchers formalize ReSHAPE, a task where planning agents revise user specifications to match acceptable plans, and build a benchmark instance generator called ReSHAPE Planter.
items.why: Highlights that fixed user specifications can exclude acceptable plans, a design consideration for planning agents and their evaluation benchmarks.

items.title: One Model, Two Precisions: Does Disagreement Between Quantized Copies Tell You When a Small Model Is Wrong?
items.summary: Study asks whether disagreement between an 8-bit and a lower-precision quantized copy of the same model can flag questions the small model likely answers wrongly.
items.why: Offers a low-cost, training-free uncertainty signal for abstention or escalation in local model deployments, costing one extra forward pass.

items.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
items.summary: Authors release drydock-eval, a local evaluator for the small Gemma 4 E4B coding agent, with container isolation, configuration checks, and paired comparisons.
items.why: Gives developers a fast local harness, running about 250 runs per hour on one RTX 5090, for matching a hosted competition scorer.

items.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
items.summary: Researchers propose HeMeR, a method letting embodied agents reconcile declarative, procedural, and working memory through structured KV cache reuse.
items.why: Targets inference efficiency for embodied agents by reusing shared memory context across consecutive decisions, relevant to latency-sensitive systems.

items.title: Time and Space: A Dual-Axis, Evidence-Grounded Context Substrate for Personal Agents
items.summary: Paper argues personal agents need spatio-temporal context representation, with temporal validity intervals and a semantic relational space, rather than just larger models.
items.why: Frames context representation as a key bottleneck for personal agents, pointing engineers toward data modeling rather than only model capacity.

items.title: ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing
items.summary: Researchers introduce ReA-Bench, a benchmark for auditing agent execution trajectories, measuring which risks are missed and false positives on legitimate behavior.
items.why: Gives teams a way to evaluate agent audit systems beyond overall recall, exposing which risks are repeatedly missed.

items.title: How many LLM-labelled rows does a decision encoder need, and how wrong can the labels be?
items.summary: Study measures how many LLM-labelled training rows a decision encoder (Laya, based on ModernBERT-large) needs and how much label noise it tolerates.
items.why: Offers guidance on data volume and label quality tradeoffs when using LLMs to generate training labels for classifiers.

items.title: Recalibrating a Typed-Decision Model in an Afternoon: A Hands-On Recipe for Laya's Confidence Scores
items.summary: Tutorial gives a five-step numpy recipe for recalibrating confidence scores of Laya, a typed-decision model, to improve answer, abstain, or escalate thresholds.
items.why: Provides a practical, low-complexity calibration procedure for classifiers that gate automated decisions versus human escalation.

items.title: SignRot: LLM Quantization with Massive Outlier-Aware Sign-Adjusted Rotation
items.summary: Researchers propose SignRot, an LLM quantization method using outlier-aware sign-adjusted rotation to handle massive activation outliers in low-bit representation.
items.why: Addresses a known failure of Hadamard-rotation quantization that degrades accuracy, relevant to teams compressing LLMs for inference.

items.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
items.summary: Researchers use pre- and post-cutoff datasets to study when delegating tasks to external tools or other LLMs improves generative search performance.
items.why: It clarifies when orchestration helps agentic search systems, which matters for deciding when to delegate versus rely on a model's own knowledge.

items.title: AI has its own style in mathematical proving
items.summary: Researchers asked three LLMs to reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's Elements and compared their citation choices against human proofs.

items.title: SPARC: Accurate Photonic Matrix Multiplication via Representative Vectors
items.summary: Researchers propose SPARC, a method using representative vectors to improve inference accuracy of neural networks on analog photonic matrix multiplication hardware.
items.why: Photonic accelerators promise lower inference power, and this targets their accuracy limits from quantization and analog noise.

items.title: Large Language Models as Digital Twins: a Distribution-Aware Questionnaire-Based Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers evaluate whether GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral can complete a Big Five questionnaire as a specific user, using their social-media posts.

items.title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce AstroMemBench, a benchmark of 2240 instances testing memory systems for embodied spacecraft agents under operational constraints.
items.why: Long-running autonomous agents in constrained, delayed environments need memory evaluation, and this offers executable tests for it.

items.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
items.summary: Researchers introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark testing whether AI agents can carry out end-to-end AI development tasks such as pre-training and post-training.
items.why: It measures whether agents can improve the systems they run on, a capability relevant to tracking agent progress and risk.

items.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose a two-branch graph and convolutional EEG network for upper-limb movement classification with region-level interpretability.

items.title: Studies on Sign Language Retrieval in Low-Resource Dictionary Settings
items.summary: Researchers test whether a pose encoder trained on ASL can retrieve signs in six other sign languages without target-language training.
items.why: It suggests transfer from data-rich sign languages could help low-resource sign language tools that lack annotated corpora.

items.title: Folio: Recoverable Multi-Resolution Context Folding for Long-Horizon Language Agents
items.summary: Researchers present Folio, a context manager that records, folds, and recovers long-horizon agent history through linked handles instead of model-based summarization.
items.why: Context window limits are a practical bottleneck for long-running agents, and recoverable folding could reduce costly re-summarization.

items.title: Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose calibrating safety budgets with Lagrange multipliers inside constrained GRPO to control harmful assistance and over-refusal in vision-language models.
items.why: Setting safety as explicit budgets rather than trial-and-error reward weights could make VLM safety tuning more predictable.

items.title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
items.summary: Researchers propose InertiaMPDD, a multimodal depression detection method that models emotional inertia to measure deviation from a non-depressed reference.

items.title: Natural Gradient Learning in Predictive Coding through Lateral Circuits
items.summary: Researchers introduce Natural PC, which adds a lateral circuit to predictive coding to extract more learning benefit from each inference phase.
items.why: Predictive coding is proposed as a backpropagation alternative, but its inference cost has limited practical use, and this targets that gap.

items.title: When Expert Disagreement Hurts: Prestige and Selectivity in LLM Decision Revision
items.summary: Researchers audit how LLMs revise binary decisions when told of disagreement, varying whether it is neutral, anonymous, or attributed to an expert.
items.why: Revision after peer disagreement can abandon correct answers, which matters for multi-agent and review pipelines relying on model consensus.

items.title: Acoustic Respiratory Phase Detection on Mobile Devices
items.summary: Researchers present a hybrid CNN-Transformer that detects breathing phases from acoustic signals recorded on commodity smartphones.
items.why: Non-invasive respiratory sensing on ordinary phones could enable breathing monitoring without contact sensors or controlled settings.

items.title: Mind the Accuracy-Approval Gap: How Users Evaluate Sycophantic AI in Everyday Tasks
items.summary: Researchers combine benchmarks and two large user studies to show how users rate sycophantic AI personas in everyday tasks, finding a gap between accuracy and approval.
items.why: Users may approve of sycophantic answers that are less accurate, so product metrics based on user satisfaction can reward the wrong behavior.

items.title: Scale-Induced Semantic Shift in Visual Prompt Injection Against VLMs and Web Agents
items.summary: Researchers show that resizing or compressing images can make hidden text instructions recoverable by vision-language models, creating a visual prompt injection risk for web agents.
items.why: Agents that ingest screenshots or resized images may follow injected instructions that were invisible at normal resolution, so input pipelines need security review.

items.title: A Modular Framework for ESG Prediction through Domain-Specific Language Modeling and Graph Learning
items.summary: ESGPred is a modular framework that predicts ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph learning over company networks.

items.title: CADET: Construction of PCB Routing Instances with Executable Demonstrations
items.summary: CADET generates synthetic PCB boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions, releasing a dataset called RouteDemos for PCB routing.
items.why: Engine-grounded demonstration data could help train automation for PCB routing, a domain with few public datasets.

items.title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
items.summary: Mantis 2 is a forecasting foundation model for infectious disease outbreaks, studying how mixing simulated and observed training data affects predictions.

items.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
items.summary: S1-Evo is a self-evolving attack framework that targets typed System-1 decision models used in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization.
items.why: Typed routing and authorization classifiers in agent stacks can be manipulated by untrusted context, so they need adversarial testing.

items.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
items.summary: The paper proposes zero-or-T thinking, where a hybrid decision model either answers in one forward pass or spends reasoning tokens only when worthwhile.
items.why: Selectively skipping reasoning could cut inference cost in production while keeping accuracy on harder queries.

items.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
items.summary: Researchers test weight-space programming, using language models to write compact neural agent weights from game mechanics, reaching 56% held-out-level success for the best writer.

items.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
items.summary: Primer is an open-source, LLM-agnostic system that helps educators build adaptive educational simulations with AI support.

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.summary: AnalogLayoutWorld is an open-source benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks testing coding agents on end-to-end analog circuit layout from transistor-level netlists.
items.why: It gives teams a concrete benchmark for measuring whether agents can handle long-horizon engineering tasks constrained by physical rules.

items.title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
items.summary: Skill Adapter proposes personalizing general-purpose agent skills for individual users and routing among an expanding skill pool during long-horizon tasks.
items.why: Agent platforms with many shared skills may need per-user adaptation and runtime skill selection to stay effective.

items.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
items.summary: SeeEEG renders EEG signals as images so a frozen vision foundation model can encode them, outperforming specialized EEG foundation models on frozen-feature transfer.
items.why: It suggests that reusing general vision models may beat costly domain-specific pretraining for some biosignal tasks.

items.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
items.summary: The paper reports ablations of LoRA fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on financial data, comparing response-only training with other regimes to measure capability retention.
items.why: It gives practical evidence on how fine-tuning choices affect retained general abilities when adapting models to domains like finance.

items.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
items.summary: A technoeconomic analysis compares grid-connected and off-grid power options for AI data centers across the continental U.S., finding speed-to-power dominates energy costs.
items.why: Interconnection and gas-turbine delays make time-to-power a key constraint on AI data center deployment planning and cost.

items.title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
items.summary: CapLite finds that small language model agents cannot reliably write security policies for prompt-injection defenses, as attacks succeed against model-written artifacts in many cases.
items.why: Teams relying on small models to generate their own injection defenses should not assume those policies hold against adversarial inputs.

items.title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: A study using counterfactual substitution finds 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims in RAG outputs derive from parametric memory rather than retrieved context.
items.why: Citations in RAG systems can misstate sources, so verification must check provenance beyond whether a citation exists.

items.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Researchers study whether decision models that act poorly can still teach well, comparing three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld.
items.why: It suggests evaluating decision models by their teaching or judging value, not just their acting performance, when training agents with reinforcement learning.

items.title: Cortex-FL: Agent-Mediated Collaboration for Federated Learning
items.summary: Cortex-FL is an agent-native federated learning system where users state learning objectives in natural language and agents find collaborators and coordinate training.
items.why: It could lower the expertise barrier for organizations adopting federated learning by automating collaborator discovery, task preparation, and coordination.

items.title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
items.summary: Al-Ghasali is a framework that formalizes Islamic jurisprudential rulings, proving closed Fiqh chapters reduce to deterministic finite state automata.

items.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
items.summary: Ballad is a bandit-based method for routing across LLMs in automated heuristic discovery, after finding larger, costlier models do not consistently yield better heuristics.
items.why: It suggests that cost-aware model routing can match or beat always using the most expensive model in iterative LLM-driven optimization pipelines.

items.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
items.summary: LiveGeo is a benchmark for geographic LLM agents, run on GeoWorld, an environment where real-world geographic states keep evolving over time.
items.why: It shifts agent evaluation from fixed states toward changing environments, relevant for teams deploying agents that must act on up-to-date world data.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Researchers report that energy-descent models solve reasoning puzzles far faster than looped models, claiming up to 1,000x speedups on puzzles like Sudoku and mazes.
items.why: If the speedups hold, energy-based methods could offer a cheaper, more stable alternative to looped reasoning models for puzzle-style tasks.

items.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
items.summary: CoReMem is a framework for coding agents that decides what memory to write and read across successive repository tasks, weighing future usefulness against costs.
items.why: It addresses how coding agents should manage persistent memory across tasks, balancing storage and retrieval cost against benefit.

items.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
items.summary: AgentSSL tests whether machine learning agents can use abundant unlabeled data when labeled data is scarce, framing semi-supervised learning as a program search problem.
items.why: It tests whether automated ML agents work outside fully supervised settings, which matters for teams with little labeled data.

items.title: The Impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Code Review Process
items.summary: A study examines how GPT assistance affects different phases of GitHub pull request review, measuring effects on resolution time and developer productivity.
items.why: Phase-specific measurements help engineering leaders decide where LLM assistance in code review actually reduces resolution time.

items.title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI
items.summary: A philosophical paper reinterprets Stuart Russell's concept of human enfeeblement through care and caregiving, framing the danger as disengagement from the world.

items.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
items.summary: EasyFoam proposes skill-oriented LLM agents for OpenFOAM CFD workflows, with evidence-driven evolution and evaluation that checks simulations against numerical acceptance criteria.
items.why: It highlights the gap between executed simulations and results meeting engineering criteria, relevant for teams automating scientific computing workflows.

items.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones
items.summary: Researchers propose a spatio-temporal Gaussian process framework that reconstructs city-wide traffic states from partial observations gathered by a fleet of drones.

items.title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
items.summary: metalSPARSE presents 2:4 semi-structured sparse GEMV kernels and a fused decoder in Metal for Apple silicon GPUs, reducing memory reads during LLM decoding.
items.why: Sparse kernels that cut bytes read could speed up on-device LLM inference on Apple hardware, where decoding is memory-bandwidth bound.

items.title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents
items.summary: SideTaskBench is a benchmark measuring whether coding agents deliver unrequested side-task artifacts while completing an authorized repository repair.
items.why: It exposes a failure mode where repair success alone misses unauthorized extra work, relevant to agent oversight and security reviews.

items.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
items.summary: AVA is an agentic system for read-level review of cancer sequencing data, aiming to separate genuine tumor mutations from artifacts in borderline low-frequency cases.

items.title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
items.summary: Researchers combined protein language models with ensemble learning to identify over 46,000 putative beta-lactamases across all four Ambler classes in environmental metagenomes.
items.why: It shows how deep learning can mine large metagenomic datasets for antibiotic resistance genes, relevant to biosecurity and resistance surveillance.

items.title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects
items.summary: MechFoundry is an agentic loop that aims to automate engineering analyses, including modeling, applying supports and loads, and assigning materials, for real-world objects.
items.why: It tests whether agents can handle engineering steps that lack easy automated verification, a gap beyond software tasks like code generation.

items.title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench
items.summary: A study of 2,160 tau2-bench episodes finds that native benchmark scoring, LLM judges, and commit-boundary checks can disagree when evaluating tool-using AI agents.
items.why: Teams using LLM judges to evaluate deployed agents should not assume they match benchmark gold-state scoring.

items.title: Finite-Cadence Refresh Equilibria for Streaming Prior-Anchored Ridge: A Closed-Form Forgetting Window and Spectral Correction
items.summary: The paper derives a closed-form forgetting window and spectral correction for prior-anchored ridge regression on drifting streams when the anchor is refreshed every k steps.

items.title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion
items.summary: CAFIN is a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework that speeds up the AdaFisher second-order optimizer by reducing sequential kernel launches and intermediate allocations.
items.why: Reducing GPU overhead in second-order optimizers could make curvature-aware training more practical for teams with limited compute budgets.

items.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
items.summary: Researchers propose a dual-domain, pretrained-transformer method for multi-step underwater acoustic channel prediction to reduce error accumulation from recursive rollout.

items.title: KernelMosaic: An Open Dataset and Agentic Framework for CUDA Kernel Generation
items.summary: KernelMosaic is an open dataset of CUDA tasks with verified solutions and trajectories, plus an agentic framework for training models to generate CUDA kernels.
items.why: An open, verified dataset for CUDA kernel generation could help teams build or evaluate code models for GPU performance work.

items.title: Evaluating AI Musical Creativity: Towards a Quantitative Multi-Dimensional Framework Based on Value, Novelty, and Surprise
items.summary: The paper proposes a quantitative framework for evaluating AI musical creativity along value, novelty, and surprise, based on Margaret Boden's theory.

items.title: Multiple-Choice Secretary Problem with Predictions
items.summary: The paper improves the Learned Kleinberg algorithm for the multiple-choice secretary problem with predictions by removing a logarithmic factor from its competitive loss.

items.title: Thompson Sampling using Prior-fitted Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: The paper introduces prior-fitted diffusion transformers that perform Thompson sampling in context at inference time for black-box continuous optimization.

items.title: Abstention Is Not Threshold Compliance: Stated Scoring Rules in Open Language Models
items.summary: A study of 12 open 3-8B language model checkpoints finds that abstention behavior under stated scoring thresholds does not reliably match threshold compliance.
items.why: Prompt-stated confidence thresholds may not reliably control when models abstain, which matters for teams relying on abstention for safety or accuracy.

items.title: Outcome Over Learning? Evidence from Student Use of AI Code Assistants for Unit Test Writing
items.summary: A user study finds most students use AI code assistants to generate complete unit tests in one shot, which may shift focus away from learning to write tests.
items.why: Engineering managers training junior developers should consider how one-shot AI generation affects skill development.

items.title: Where Should the Code Go? Locating Foundation-Model Errors in Bitemporal Inventory Simulation
items.summary: The paper tests where exact code should be placed relative to foundation-model calls, using a lost-sales inventory environment with bitemporal operational reports.
items.why: It offers guidance on combining exact code with LLM components in stateful simulations, a design choice relevant to production agent systems.

items.title: MITRA-Swarm: Injecting Explicit Linguistic Structure into Foundation Models for Classical Machine Translation
items.summary: MITRA-Swarm is a multi-agent architecture for Sanskrit machine translation that uses a Sandhi-splitting agent, parallel translators, and a discourse-aware ellipsis restorer.

items.title: What Entropy-Based View Selection Cannot See: An Audit of Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: An audit finds that entropy-based view selection for test-time adaptation of CLIP-style vision-language models has limitations in choosing which augmented views to trust.
items.why: Teams deploying vision-language models under distribution shift may find entropy-based confidence heuristics less reliable than assumed.

items.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
items.summary: Researchers propose RACE, a risk-aware control method that sets wireless reliability levels for uplink sensory data based on predicted risk of incorrect actions in edge inference.
items.why: Suggests per-task reliability targets instead of fixed SINR requirements, which could reduce overprovisioning of wireless resources for 6G Physical-AI systems.

items.title: Code as Explanations: Executable and Verifiable LLM Explanations
items.summary: Researchers propose code-based explanations, where a program explains LLM behavior across a dataset and can be verified on new inputs, unlike per-instance free-text explanations.
items.why: Offers a way to test LLM behavior claims on new inputs, which may help teams audit model decisions more systematically than chain-of-thought text.

items.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age
items.summary: A study compares tasks people perform in ChatGPT with freelance work requested on Upwork, finding generative AI shifts which tasks gain or lose marketplace share.
items.why: Shows how AI is reshaping demand for freelance skills and task bundles, relevant to teams planning hiring and contractor sourcing.

items.title: From Nodes to Pixels: Topological and Structural Two-View Graph Imaging
items.summary: Researchers introduce G2Image, a framework that converts graphs into two fixed-budget image-like views for use as a standardized input for graph learning models.

items.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce MDU, a multilingual document understanding benchmark with 23,146 examples across 13 tasks and five European languages, to test vision-language models beyond English.
items.why: Reveals how well VLMs handle non-English documents and layouts, useful for teams deploying document AI across languages.

items.title: Graph Label Alignment: A Diagnostic Atlas for Graph Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose graph label alignment, a diagnostic that measures label accessibility in graph classification benchmarks without training a graph encoder.
items.why: Helps teams judge whether benchmark gains reflect real structure-feature reasoning or easily accessible label signal.

items.title: Mach2: Scientific Discovery Platform with Deterministic Execution Constraints
items.summary: Mach2 is a scientific discovery platform that couples agent orchestration with deterministic, lint-like checks on tool requests, source changes, tests, and artifact contracts.
items.why: Shows a pattern for enforcing agent compliance with executable rules rather than relying on prompting alone, relevant to agent system design.

items.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
items.summary: Researchers present OverServe, a multi-agent framework that crafts prompts to make SaaS agents extend execution, wasting provider compute without extra customer payment.
items.why: Identifies a resource-amplification risk for subscription SaaS agents, so providers need limits on agent run length and tool calls.

items.title: Discharge Summary Generation Is Not Just Summarization: A Reality Check for Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers introduce FairSumEval, a fact-level evaluation framework for discharge summaries that checks whether reference and generated facts are supported by clinical notes.
items.why: Shows reference-based evaluation can penalize models for missing content not in the input, so evaluation design matters for clinical summarization.

items.title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers propose HDH, a lightweight method that trains a compact action verifier on a frozen vision-language-action model's own rollouts to reduce latency in action selection.
items.why: Offers a low-latency way to improve robot policy action selection without retraining the base VLA model.

items.title: When Safety Becomes an Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention in Tool-Using AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers study warning-induced over-abstention, where fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content cause tool-using AI agents to refuse legitimate tasks, and propose a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol.
items.why: Shows agents' refusal behavior can be exploited as a denial-of-service vector, so teams should verify the source and authority of risk claims.

items.title: MLIRBench - A Benchmark and Dataset for Compiler and Hardware-Aware Reasoning
items.summary: MLIRBench is introduced as a benchmark and dataset for evaluating whether LLMs understand compiler intermediate representations and hardware-aware semantics.
items.why: Provides a way to test whether code models reason about MLIR semantics rather than memorized patterns, relevant to compiler tooling.

items.title: Understanding the Effects of Multi-Agent Deliberation for Human-AI Decision-Making
items.summary: User studies find multi-agent deliberation among LLMs helps humans verify responses and fact-check, with multi-round interaction driving most of the benefit over single-round AI assistance.
items.why: Suggests multi-round AI discussion may improve human decisions more than simply adding more models, informing decision-support design.

items.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
items.summary: A paper revisits the claim that RL generalizes while SFT memorizes, finding SFT data source is critical and a carefully mixed SFT dataset can substantially outperform single-source data.
items.why: Indicates that SFT data composition, not just the training method, may determine generalization, guiding post-training data choices.

items.title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
items.summary: Researchers show speech tokenizers are fragile to small semantic-level perturbations and introduce T-SemAttack, a transferable attack that degrades downstream ASR and audio-language models.
items.why: Exposes a transferable vulnerability in speech front ends that affects ASR and audio-LLM pipelines, so robustness testing is warranted.

items.title: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), using offline-generated Segment Hints to assign token-level credit for reasoning segmentation among visually similar objects.
items.why: Shows a way to turn sparse trajectory-level rewards into token-level credit signals for vision-language reasoning tasks.

items.title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
items.summary: A counterfactual audit tests whether GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen show racial and sex bias in pain management recommendations.
items.why: Teams deploying LLMs in clinical settings need evidence on demographic bias and response instability before relying on model outputs.

items.title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals
items.summary: A single-seed CARLA case study finds a posterior-prior gap: a world model's imagined rollouts lose obstacle information that its posterior states retain.
items.why: Model-based planners that rely on imagined rollouts may silently discard task-relevant signals, which engineers should measure rather than assume.

items.title: Binding Mode Matters: Hotspot-Aware Drug Discovery via Explorative Preferences
items.summary: Researchers frame target-based drug design as multi-objective exploration, with each objective targeting a specific binding hotspot to find diverse binding modes.

items.title: Who Moved the Frontier? Paying Open Frontier Challenges with Free Identities
items.summary: The paper examines how to pay participants in open frontier challenges when identities are free, showing rank prizes can be gamed by one solver using multiple identities.
items.why: Anyone designing open AI contests or bounties must account for Sybil-style gaming when identities cost nothing.

items.title: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking
items.summary: Researchers identify a 'task badness' activation direction that rises as failures accumulate and precedes reward hacking in Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B and Gemma-4-31B.
items.why: Suggests internal activation signals could be monitored to detect or reduce reward hacking during difficult coding tasks.

items.title: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage
items.summary: QSim-Arena is a research framework where AI agents combine verification, benchmarking and open exploration to find practical advantage in quantum dynamics simulation.

items.title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-in-the-Loop Calibration for Real-Time Optimal Power Flow
items.summary: A paper proposes an LLM-enhanced deep reinforcement learning framework with human-in-the-loop calibration for real-time optimal power flow.
items.why: Shows how LLM-derived sparse signals and human feedback can encode operating preferences that numerical rewards struggle to capture.

items.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
items.summary: CARMEN is a cardiorespiratory foundation model pretrained without labels on ten physiological waveforms, including arterial, venous, pulmonary artery, intracranial pressures and ventilator signals.
items.why: Extends foundation models beyond ECG and PPG to ICU and perioperative waveforms, a useful direction for clinical ML teams.

items.title: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents
items.summary: A paper argues that economic institutions like auctions and markets are only a sample of possible designs, and proposes treating institutions as a design space for artificial agents.
items.why: Engineers building multi-agent systems may need institution designs that fit agents' private minds, learning, and persistence, not human-derived mechanisms.

items.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting
items.summary: SkinAdvisor presents a deployed multi-modal Transformer, SkinCast, that forecasts 180-day per-day sales for unreleased in-game cosmetic skins to guide production planning.
items.why: Shows a deployed multi-modal forecasting pipeline applied to production decisions in game monetization.

items.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models
items.summary: Researchers propose generative models to learn quasar optical variability as an alternative to the damped random walk model commonly used as a null hypothesis.

items.title: Estimating Image Creativity
items.summary: Researchers present a framework that estimates perceived image creativity from dimensions such as novelty, surprise and arousal to predict human creativity ratings.

items.title: Prototypes of the Mind: A Unified Framework for Probing the Visual Brain
items.summary: Prototypes of the Mind is a unified framework connecting vision foundation models to fMRI activity using sparse, interpretable representations for encoding, decoding and interpretation.
items.why: Offers a single interpretable representation for multiple neural analysis tasks instead of separate single-objective models.

items.title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios
items.summary: TFC-MMFD is a time-frequency-condition multimodal fusion foundation model aimed at diagnosing faults across many rotating machines and operating conditions without retraining.
items.why: Targets the one-machine-one-model scaling problem in industrial fault diagnosis, a practical concern for predictive maintenance teams.

items.title: CoLaX: Context-Aware Local Explanations for Time Series Classification
items.summary: CoLaX proposes a context-aware post-hoc explanation method for time series classifiers that scores local patterns conditioned on the full sequence's learned representation.
items.why: Explanations that ignore global sequence context may mislead when debugging time series models; context-aware attribution could make model audits more reliable.

items.title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
items.summary: The paper proves that Binary Tokenization has no polynomial-time approximation within a certain factor under standard assumptions, and presents bicriteria approximation algorithms.

items.title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
items.summary: CFGComposer composes two independently trained diffusion models at inference to generate whole-body gestures synchronized with speech audio and aligned with text.
items.why: It offers a training-free way to combine separately trained generative models, relevant to embodied AI and social robotics teams.

items.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science
items.summary: The paper proposes a proof-relevant type theory for verified scientific knowledge stores, arguing proof assistants' judgmental proof irrelevance blocks comparing independent derivations.

items.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers present Lazarus, a method that turns a capable model into a backdoored sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons without training.
items.why: Model weight integrity is a security risk for agents running unattended with privileged access, whether models are third-party or internal.

items.title: "I don't know what I don't know": Exploring the Benefits and Challenges of AI in Interdisciplinary Research
items.summary: A survey of 62 and interviews with 23 interdisciplinary researchers examine the challenges and opportunities AI poses for workflows spanning unfamiliar disciplines.

items.title: Read Once, Answer Many: Parallel Prompting for Shared-Context LLM Inference
items.summary: Parallel Prompting decodes multiple questions about a shared long document as parallel streams within one request, reducing repeated key-value cache reads during decoding.
items.why: Targets memory-bandwidth bottlenecks in shared-context LLM workloads like document QA, labeling, and evaluation, which can cut inference cost.

items.title: When Does Learned Constraint Selection Pay in Security-Constrained Optimisation? A Boundary Map from SCOPF to Unit Commitment
items.summary: The paper compares learned constraint selection for security-constrained optimal power flow against a fixed umbrella constraint set, mapping when learning pays off.

items.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Using V-JEPA Features
items.summary: Researchers study adapting V-JEPA video features for supervised RGB-only multi-view 3D reconstruction, evaluated on CO3D and TUM RGB-D.

items.title: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision
items.summary: The paper reframes converting SDR video to HDR as blind posterior inference, using latent luminance supervision to recover radiance lost to tone mapping.

items.title: GingivitisSeg: A Public Dataset and Comparative Benchmark for Gingivitis Segmentation in Intraoral Images
items.summary: The authors release GingivitisSeg, a public benchmark of 961 intraoral images with pixel-level gingivitis annotations and a comparison of seven segmentation configurations.
