items.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
items.summary: The paper introduces a training-free framework for personalized image segmentation, arguing prior strong results largely stem from evaluation artifacts.
items.why: Suggests current benchmark numbers for instance-level segmentation may be overstated, relevant to teams evaluating vision systems.

items.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather
items.summary: The paper examines challenges for robust automated driving in extreme weather such as snow, rain, and fog, which remain understudied relative to clear conditions.
items.why: Highlights that perception and control performance degrades in harsh weather, a key gap for autonomous vehicle deployment.

items.title: Fr\'echetFlow: Flow Matching for Non-Euclidean Data
items.summary: FréchetFlow extends flow matching to generative modeling for metric space-valued data such as distributions, trees, and covariance matrices without requiring linear operations or manifold structure.
items.why: Offers a generative approach for non-Euclidean data types that standard flow matching methods cannot handle directly.

items.title: KQML-Liver: Interpretable Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Liver Disease Classification
items.summary: KQML-Liver is a hybrid quantum machine learning framework using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for interpretable liver disease classification.

items.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
items.summary: Researchers propose DredRL, a dual-representation diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler for flexible job-shop scheduling under scale and processing-time uncertainty.
items.why: Shows diffusion policies being applied to manufacturing scheduling, a niche where uncertainty often breaks existing DRL approaches.

items.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
items.summary: Researchers introduce a multi-head quantum neural network that replaces transformer blocks inside a 30-billion-parameter LLM, claiming little accuracy loss with far fewer parameters.
items.why: Suggests a path to reducing LLM parameter counts using NISQ-compatible quantum modules, though practical hardware readiness remains unclear from the abstract.

items.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.summary: Researchers present CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets.
items.why: Offers a benchmark for evaluating forecasting agents on context use and adaptive interaction, not just numerical accuracy.

items.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
items.summary: Researchers study whether a small open Gemma 4 12B customer-service agent can improve its policy adherence and consistency from its own deployment logs without a stronger teacher model.
items.why: Points to a self-improvement method for small private-deployment agents that could reduce reliance on frontier models.

items.title: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction
items.summary: Researchers evaluate quantum-classical hybrid recurrent models, QLSTM and quantum reservoir computing, for financial time-series forecasting.
items.why: Provides an early benchmark of quantum recurrent models on financial forecasting, though the abstract gives no clear performance advantage.

items.title: Matrix-Based Ant Colony Search with Batched Decoding for Hierarchical Replenishment Routing: A Stylized Case Study Based on Korean City Data
items.summary: Researchers propose a matrix-based ant colony search with batched decoding for a stylized replenishment-routing problem built on Korean city data.

items.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
items.summary: Researchers release Breath-Dx, a benchmark for time series classification of electronic-nose data for disease screening, including sensor drift.
items.why: Offers a standardized benchmark for eNose disease screening that accounts for sensor drift, a common failure mode in the field.

items.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
items.summary: Researchers present CARE-Drive, a method that refines ego-vehicle trajectories in vision-language-action autonomous driving models by coupling physical quantities during refinement.
items.why: Targets trajectory quality in end-to-end VLA driving models, a relevant direction for autonomous-driving system builders.

items.title: Is the Importance Ratio Necessary for Stable Reinforcement Learning in LLMs?
items.summary: Researchers propose LGPO, an RL method for LLM post-training that uses likelihood-based gating instead of importance sampling ratios, removing the need for old-policy likelihoods.
items.why: If the claim holds, it cuts compute overhead in GRPO-style LLM post-training by dropping old-policy likelihood computation.

items.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
items.summary: Researchers introduce SimRec, an RL framework that trains the full interaction policy of tool-integrated LLM recommendation agents using a simulated user.
items.why: Shows training whole agent interaction policies rather than isolated components, relevant to building tool-using recommendation agents.

items.title: TopoST: Topology-Conditioned Node Specialization for Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models
items.summary: Researchers propose TopoST, a urban spatio-temporal foundation model that shares learning over local subgraphs with topology-conditioned node specialization.
items.why: Offers a transfer approach for urban spatio-temporal models across heterogeneous datasets, though applicability beyond urban settings is unclear.

items.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce ReasonText and a diagnostic study arguing that text-aware image super-resolution benefits from reasoning over image context, not just visual restoration.
items.why: Suggests reasoning components may be needed for restoring severely degraded text, challenging purely visual restoration pipelines.

items.title: WaveFlow-UIE: A Single-Pipeline Wavelet-Domain Flow Model for Efficient Underwater Image Restoration
items.summary: Researchers present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model for underwater image restoration that avoids multi-stage diffusion pipelines.
items.why: Offers a lighter alternative to costly multi-stage diffusion restoration, relevant for efficiency-constrained imaging systems.

items.title: Right Answers, Inconsistent Evidence: Source-Level Counterfactual Auditing of Large Audio-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce TRACE, a counterfactual auditing method showing 6.3% of correct answers from 8 large audio-language models rely on inconsistent evidence.
items.why: Reveals that correct audio-LLM answers can mask unreliable evidence use, a concern for evaluating multimodal systems beyond accuracy.

items.title: AutoOntic: Automatic Ontology Induction from Text for Knowledge Graph Construction
items.summary: Researchers present AutoOntic, a pipeline that automatically induces an ontology from text, adding type hierarchies and relation domain/range constraints to knowledge graphs.
items.why: Could improve graph-based RAG by producing typed, constrained knowledge graphs instead of flat extractions.

items.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
items.summary: Researchers propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability of reinforcement learning policies to high-dimensional, multi-action settings.
items.why: Offers a way to make deep RL policies more interpretable in complex action spaces, which matters for trust in deployed agents.

items.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Researchers introduce DecArena, a benchmark for evaluating decentralized multi-agent collaboration where agents discover non-local resources under graph-constrained communication.
items.why: Points to how multi-agent systems might scale without a global orchestrator, relevant to privacy and scalability design.

items.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
items.summary: Researchers released GHAgentCI, a dataset of coding-agent invocations found in GitHub Actions workflow histories across thousands of mined repositories.
items.why: Gives teams a data source for understanding how coding agents are already embedded in CI pipelines and their execution constraints.

items.title: An Approach to Hinton's Mother-Child Proposal: Neural Networks Learning and Preserving Care in a Finite World
items.summary: The paper explores Hinton's proposal of AI with maternal instincts, arguing care must be learned by the network and tested for survival in a finite world.

items.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
items.summary: Researchers present MAGIC, a method for detecting clinical hallucinations in medical large multimodal models using modality-aware distribution analysis.
items.why: Addresses a reliability gap for medical LMMs, where unverifiable confident outputs pose serious risks in high-stakes settings.

items.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
items.summary: Researchers propose a query decomposition approach to improve generalization and citation accuracy in attributable retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop questions.
items.why: Targets over-citation and entity identification failures in RAG, which matter for verifiable answers in production systems.

items.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
items.summary: Researchers introduce isloss, a deterministic rule-based oracle that detects silent information loss, such as dropped roles or tool interactions, when translating conversations across LLM APIs.
items.why: Gives teams a testable way to catch silent data loss in API translation layers and compatibility shims.

items.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
items.summary: TraceKV proposes a policy-preserving low-rank KV cache compression method for reasoning vision-language models to reduce memory demands without reasoning failures.
items.why: Reducing KV cache memory while preserving reasoning accuracy directly affects serving cost and feasibility for multimodal reasoning models.

items.title: Can Model Answer Probabilities Represent Survey Populations? Conditional Prediction and Joint Validity in Jev Survey Simulation
items.summary: Researchers evaluate whether option probabilities from the Jev decision model can represent survey populations, testing conditional prediction and joint validity across linked survey responses.

items.title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
items.summary: Researchers introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation method for industrial inspection robots that aims to reduce computational and storage costs.
items.why: Lower onboard compute needs for multi-scale navigation could matter for robots operating where wireless coverage is incomplete.

items.title: Bug Finding With Agentic Symbolic Execution
items.summary: Researchers present an agentic harness that pairs the CrossHair symbolic execution tool with an AI coding agent to find Python bugs without human-written assertions.
items.why: Combining symbolic execution with coding agents could reduce the manual effort needed to adopt bug-finding tools in real repositories.

items.title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
items.summary: Researchers study data scaling for universal machine-learned interatomic potentials, comparing M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined 1.16-million-structure dataset.
items.why: Shows that equal dataset sizes may not yield equal value, informing how teams budget expensive training data for scientific models.

items.title: Contrastive Bootstrap Representation Learning for Label-Efficient Agricultural Image Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose ContrastBoot, a label-efficient representation learning method combining contrastive and bootstrap signals for agricultural image classification under label scarcity.
items.why: Shows a route to strong image classifiers when expert labels are scarce and costly, a common constraint in specialized domains.

items.title: Learning-Based Interpolation of Detector Gaps in Photon-Counting X-ray Imaging
items.summary: Researchers adapt WGAN-GP and Pix2Pix generative models to interpolate gaps between tiled detector modules in photon-counting X-ray imaging.

items.title: Data-Free Metrics Don't Work: The Missing Invariance Under Functionally Preserving Reparameterisations
items.summary: The paper argues that data-free random matrix theory metrics for layer quality fail to remain invariant under functionally preserving reparameterisations of neural networks.
items.why: Challenges the reliability of data-free layer metrics that some teams use to guide pre-training and model diagnosis.

items.title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers propose MemInStream, a benchmark design arguing that question-answering accuracy alone fails to measure memory in streaming video understanding.
items.why: Engineers evaluating video models should not treat QA accuracy as proof of memory, since errors and correct answers can stem from other causes.

items.title: Contour-Assisted Evolutionary Computation: Estimating Peaks From the Contour Lines of Evaluated Solutions
items.summary: Researchers propose contour-assisted evolutionary computation, treating evaluated candidate solutions as topographic spot heights to estimate peaks and maintain a memory of them.

items.title: When Agents Need to Consolidate Memories: What RRR Consolidation Explains, and What It Does Not Explain, in Conversation ESAA
items.summary: An engineering study introduces Memory-TCG, a conversation memory extension for language-model agents, comparing retrieval and consolidation methods on a synthetic evaluation.
items.why: Teams building persistent agent memory may find that stored conversation history does not guarantee retrieval of current decisions and their provenance.

items.title: AskALCF: A Self-Improving Agentic System for Intelligent HPC User Support
items.summary: AskALCF is an agentic log-analysis pipeline that evaluates production HPC user-support interactions, attributes failures to components, and improves the system after deployment.
items.why: Shows a deployment-oriented pattern for evaluating and continuously improving LLM support systems using production logs.

items.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates
items.summary: Researchers present GLOBAFED, a federated Bayesian optimization framework using neural network surrogates to share knowledge across heterogeneous clients without exposing raw data.
items.why: Offers a way to transfer optimization knowledge in privacy-sensitive settings where objectives differ, relaxing restrictive assumptions of prior methods.

items.title: Curiosity-0826-4B: Generative Medical Event Sequence Modeling Across Pediatric and Adult Populations
items.summary: Curiosity-0826-4B, an updated generative medical event foundation model trained on Epic Cosmos, is reported to match or exceed its predecessor on several clinical prediction tasks.

items.title: Outside the Purview of the Reward: Capability Drift in Multilingual Post-Training
items.summary: A study finds that GRPO post-training in a multilingual mixture-of-experts model boosted math scores while degrading Indic-language F1, with a sibling model recovering some losses.
items.why: Reward-driven post-training can silently regress capabilities users still need, so teams should evaluate beyond the optimized reward.

items.title: Terms of Care: Designing for Participation in Data Governance by Disability Communities
items.summary: Researchers worked with three disability advocacy organizations on context-sensitive licensing so disability communities can participate in governing datasets used for AI-generated media.
items.why: Highlights governance and licensing considerations for community-specific datasets that could be misused or exploited if openly shared.

items.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
items.summary: A paper offers a mechanistic account of where uncertainty is observed inside LLM computation, arguing the observation point determines which uncertainty estimators can recover targets.
items.why: Choosing where to measure uncertainty inside a model affects how reliably teams can detect unreliable LLM responses.

items.title: Latent Imagination for Parameterized Action Spaces
items.summary: Researchers introduce HyLI, a model-based agent that learns a hybrid policy in latent imagination for parameterized action spaces and acts with a single forward pass.
items.why: Offers a route to sample-efficient reinforcement learning agents that act quickly without per-step planning.

items.title: Prior-as-Skill: Remember Outside and Read Inside with On-Policy Self-Distillation for Self-Evolving VLM Agents
items.summary: Prior-as-Skill proposes on-policy self-distillation to train self-evolving vision-language agents to read stored skills, aiming to handle missing frames and reordered steps at deployment.
items.why: Addresses robustness of visual agents when stored task demonstrations are missing or reordered at deployment time.

items.title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
items.summary: Researchers release PDO drug screening data from four studies using patient-derived organoids to evaluate and train AI drug response prediction models.
items.why: Provides patient-derived rather than cell-line data, which may better match clinical targets for drug response models.

items.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
items.summary: SO-Arena is a benchmark assessing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families.
items.why: Aggregate benchmark scores can hide capability gaps and decision reliability issues that matter when choosing fast models.

items.title: Honesty Is a Race: Predicting When Verifiable-Reward RL Teaches a Model to Bluff
items.summary: A paper studies when reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards leads a model to honestly report or to bluff about unverifiable verdicts, deriving a condition for honesty under GRPO.
items.why: Reward design for code verification can incentivize models to bluff, so teams training with verifiable rewards need to check for this failure.

items.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
items.summary: VibePrevisBench is a benchmark evaluating coding agents that reconstruct 4D scenes in Blender from briefs, checking both executable scenes and rendered proxy videos across 242 tasks.
items.why: Gives a way to measure coding agents on multi-shot 4D scene generation for controllable video production workflows.

items.title: RUMI: A Robotiq-Matched Universal Manipulation Interface for Robot Learning with Augmented Reality and Haptic Feedback
items.summary: Researchers present RUMI, a handheld manipulation interface matched to the Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, with exchangeable fingertip sensors for force-aware robot data collection.
items.why: Force-aware demonstration data is scarce, and a gripper-matched handheld interface could make collecting contact-rich robot learning datasets easier.

items.title: Fine-Grained Generative Hallucination Detection and Correction for Aerial Image Captioning
items.summary: Researchers propose a fine-grained method to detect and correct hallucinations in captions generated by multimodal LLMs for UAV aerial imagery.
items.why: Hallucinated captions can mislead surveillance and disaster-response workflows, so reliable detection and correction matters for deployment.

items.title: Large Payments Model
items.summary: A paper introduces the Large Payments Model, a shared representation layer meant to support fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization.
items.why: A reusable payments model could reduce per-task model development, though the summary gives limited detail on results or deployment.

items.title: The BEATS Dataset: Towards Understanding Music-Physiology Dynamics in Real-World Scenarios
items.summary: Researchers release the BEATS dataset of psycho-physiological data from 30 participants listening to wellbeing playlists in real-world settings.

items.title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing
items.summary: Researchers propose Spec-Driven PBT, which derives semantic invariants from code specifications so LLM agents can author property-based tests for agentic coding.
items.why: As agents produce code faster than it can be reviewed, automatically derived property tests could offer a practical check on AI-written software.

items.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
items.summary: DuoJEPA trains separate self-supervised encoders per modality and adds a translation layer so embeddings can be mapped across unaligned spaces for retrieval and classification.
items.why: It suggests cross-modal tasks may not require aligning encoder embedding spaces, which could change how multimodal systems are built.

items.title: What Roles Do System Prompts Really Assign? Validating and Steering Occupational Role Vectors in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce a framework to extract and inject occupational role vectors from system prompts, testing them on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
items.why: Steering model behavior through role vectors could help teams verify that system prompts actually shape model responses as intended.

items.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
items.summary: Fit-LRP proposes exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex polytope regions to tighten neural network verification beyond axis-aligned boxes.
items.why: Tighter verification over realistic cyber-physical constraints could make safety certification of neural controllers more practical.

items.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
items.summary: A controlled study dissects designs of GPT-6 robot-use agents on RoboDojo, testing harness, action interface, experience reuse, and scene geometry in one framework.
items.why: Isolating which design choices drive gains helps engineers build robot agents without relying on confounded benchmark comparisons.

items.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
items.summary: Iris-Z proposes scaling a single generative model for vision, 3D, and spatial understanding instead of task-specific specialist models.
items.why: It argues for unified architectures over task-specific designs in computer vision, which could shape how vision systems are built and scaled.

items.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
items.summary: A theoretical paper proves an exponential runtime speedup for Cartesian Genetic Programming on the Max problem, compared with prior analyses.
items.why: Formal runtime guarantees for CGP are rare, though the work is theoretical and its direct engineering impact is limited.

items.title: Scaling public input on AI policy with pluralistic agents
items.summary: Researchers develop pluralistic agents that deliberate on behalf of individuals to gather diverse public input on AI policy and alignment.
items.why: Scalable public input mechanisms could inform how organizations incorporate diverse stakeholder perspectives into AI policy decisions.

items.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
items.summary: A paper explores whether pyramidal columns in language regions of the brain could biologically realize a Transformer attention head.
items.why: This is a theoretical neuroscience hypothesis with little direct bearing on engineering practice.

items.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match
items.summary: Researchers propose a worker-firm match quality measure learned from employment survival, using a two-tower neural network over career histories and firm descriptions.
items.why: Match-quality modeling could inform hiring and workforce analytics, though it raises fairness and privacy questions the summary does not address.

items.title: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff
items.summary: Researchers design and evaluate Solidity smart contracts for federated learning rewards, including a zero-knowledge variant that hides individual quality scores.
items.why: It shows a concrete tradeoff between privacy and fairness in incentive design for federated learning systems built on blockchain.

items.title: Agentic Computational Algebra
items.summary: Researchers propose evaluating AI agents on computational algebra tasks, where the challenge is speed rather than correctness, measuring whether agents find and exploit problem structure.
items.why: It frames a benchmark for agents optimizing computational cost, not just answer accuracy, relevant to anyone building agents for heavy numerical workloads.

items.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
items.summary: Researchers test TabPFN, a tabular foundation model, to reconstruct 2D subsurface sections from sparse cone penetration test data without geotechnical fine-tuning.
items.why: It shows a general pretrained tabular model can fill sparse-data gaps in a specialized engineering domain without task-specific training.

items.title: Show Your Work in Swahili: Reinforcement Learning for Native-Language Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: Fikiria, a two-stage SFT plus GRPO recipe, trains models for Swahili math reasoning, rewarding reasoning-trace similarity to native-language references as well as answer accuracy.
items.why: It offers a reward design for improving non-English reasoning fidelity, useful for teams building multilingual reasoning models.

items.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: A study finds content-description labelling coverage in Android GUI corpora used to train computer-use agents is low, with gaps persisting between 2017 and 2024 datasets.
items.why: Agents trained on poorly labelled interface data inherit accessibility gaps, so teams should audit training corpora and evaluate accessibility outcomes.

items.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
items.summary: ADAPT is an agentic approach that generates focused tests for pull request code changes, targeting the behavior a diff introduces rather than whole units or coverage.
items.why: Diff-aware test generation could help teams guard new PR behavior against regressions without relying on developers to write tests.

items.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
items.summary: SwarmSafe-Delta is a paired protocol that isolates how upstream messages affect an LLM agent team's policy-violating actions, comparing real delivery against placebo messages.
items.why: It gives teams a method to measure whether inter-agent messages alone cause unsafe actions, informing multi-agent safety design.

items.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
items.summary: Researchers propose a self-supervised attention-based model for virtual metrology, estimating chemical mechanical planarization material removal rate from process time series.
items.why: It reduces reliance on physical metrology and handcrafted features in semiconductor process control, relevant to industrial ML deployments.

items.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
items.summary: JudgeMix proposes judge-guided mixed-rollout data synthesis to train LLM agents, using expert assistance aware of the target model's state during rollouts.
items.why: It targets the training-inference distribution mismatch in SFT for agents, a practical concern for teams fine-tuning agent models.

items.title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous
items.summary: A paper argues that same-state positive pairs make the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis vacuous, undermining its uniqueness claim.
items.why: It challenges a theoretical justification for representation convergence in JEPA-style models, relevant mainly to researchers evaluating those foundations.

items.title: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features
items.summary: Less is Safer (LIS) is a compact safety alignment dataset built with sparse autoencoder feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis, aiming to reduce over-refusal.
items.why: A small, interpretable safety dataset could lower alignment costs and over-refusal, a practical trade-off for teams tuning deployed models.

items.title: When can an interpretability claim be trusted? Stability and certification of feature dimensionality, ridge leverage and the feature recovery rate
items.summary: The paper studies when interpretability claims, such as sparse dictionaries recovering most features, are reliable under small changes in weights, seeds, or thresholds.
items.why: Safety claims built on interpretability metrics can be fragile to thresholds and seeds, so teams should validate them before relying on them.

items.title: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models
items.summary: Researchers test whether small open language models on a laptop can generate Coccinelle semantic patches from examples of Linux kernel API conversions.
items.why: Small local models producing kernel refactoring rules could speed tree-wide API migrations, which engineers maintaining large codebases would find useful.

items.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: GRPO reinforcement learning on a 30B mixture-of-experts model improves MATH by 36.07 points but causes regressions on several Indic-language benchmarks, such as XQuAD-Indic F1 falling 19.32 points.
items.why: RL gains can come with cross-lingual regressions as answers shift to English, so teams must evaluate across languages, not just aggregate benchmarks.

items.title: Label-Efficient Document-Grounded Factuality Detection via Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning
items.summary: CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework, trains compact document-grounded factuality detectors from a small labeled set using cross-paraphrastic invariance learning.
items.why: It offers a way to build efficient factuality checkers with limited labeled data, useful for teams running hallucination detection at scale.

items.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
items.summary: Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT) redesigns feedback between loops using an interpolation schedule, aiming to prevent hidden-state scale growth in looped language models.
items.why: Looped transformers offer parameter-efficient depth, and stabilizing recurrence could make them more viable for compact language model designs.

items.title: SMIC: Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning across Transformer Layers for Natural Language Inference
items.summary: Researchers introduce SMIC, a method that builds one multiscale reference from the input and reuses it across Transformer layers for natural language inference.
items.why: It offers an architectural tweak to improve NLI robustness to localized lexical changes, though gains are only described in from-scratch comparisons.

items.title: Eliciting and Mitigating Specification Satisficing in Coding Agents
items.summary: Researchers define 'specification satisficing,' where coding agents accept implementations that miss requirements, and propose SatisFix to identify and mitigate it.
items.why: Coding agents that silently skip requirements are a reliability risk, and existing self-correction methods reportedly miss this failure mode.

items.title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
items.summary: ORCHID-SAGE is presented as a fully reproducible CALPHAD workflow that records expert decisions so thermodynamic phase diagrams can be regenerated and updated.
items.why: Recording the decisions behind materials databases makes them reproducible and updatable, which matters for self-driving lab pipelines.

items.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
items.summary: A study of 15 open-weight models on Fermi estimation finds that shared item-level error limits gains from aggregating small language model answers.
items.why: Multi-agent averaging may not reduce error as much as expected, since errors are correlated across draws for the same item.

items.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
items.summary: Researchers propose WIS-MeZO, which uses Wanda saliency to build sparse perturbation masks for memory-efficient zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs.
items.why: Sparse, task-conditioned perturbations could cut the search dimension for forward-only LLM fine-tuning, reducing memory needs.

items.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
items.summary: SUMNO is a spatially unrolled multigrid neural operator proposed as a fluid flow surrogate that aims to improve accuracy on complex flows.
items.why: Faster and more accurate CFD surrogates could reduce solver costs, though the text gives few performance details.

items.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
items.summary: DRAMA analyzes attention redundancy in multimodal diffusion LLMs to accelerate inference, where visual tokens dominate long sequences and cost per step is quadratic.
items.why: Targeting attention redundancy in multimodal diffusion LLMs addresses a real inference cost bottleneck for vision-language serving.

items.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
items.summary: HyBridge is a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method that uses bridge nodes to guide embeddings.

items.title: ReliaGuard: Reconstruction-Aware Watermarking for Source Attribution and Blind Edit Localization
items.summary: ReliaGuard is a watermarking framework that aims to support source attribution and blind edit localization for generative image edits, even after reconstruction.
items.why: Watermarks that survive VAE reconstruction could help verify provenance of AI-edited images, a concern for content platforms.

items.title: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: Persistent Latent-State Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models
items.summary: Recursive SALM adds a persistent latent state that evolves with observations and generates adaptations to a pretrained language model, evaluated with frozen GPT-2 small.
items.why: A persistent latent state could extend effective memory beyond token context, though the evaluation described is limited.

items.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
items.summary: CoMem proposes query-guided selective soft context compression, compressing only task-relevant parts of long inputs into compact memory slots.
items.why: Selective compression targets the efficiency of long-context inference, a practical cost concern for LLM deployments.

items.title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation
items.summary: TransXplainRRG is a vision-language model for chest X-ray report generation, evaluated by radiologists and designed with explainability in mind.
items.why: Clinical report generation with explainability and radiologist evaluation is relevant to healthcare AI teams weighing adoption.

items.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
items.summary: PhysCapBench is a cross-domain benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, testing whether captions capture interactions and state transitions.
items.why: Benchmarks for physical grounding in video captions can help evaluate training data quality for physical AI systems.

items.title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication
items.summary: The RMIT-ADM+S team describes seven research-agent runs for TREC 2026 RAG, finding writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion most affect answer quality.
items.why: Ablations identify writer model choice and chunk expansion as key levers for RAG answer quality.

items.title: SoScale: Second-Order Scale Search for FP4 Quantization
items.summary: SoScale proposes a second-order scale search method for FP4 quantization of LLMs, targeting formats like MXFP4, NVFP4, and HiF4.
items.why: Better FP4 scale selection could improve accuracy of low-bit LLM inference, reducing memory and serving cost.

items.title: DesignTaste: Benchmarking AI-Generator Visual Design Against Award-Wining Works
items.summary: Researchers introduced DesignTaste, a benchmark of 403 design briefs comparing text-to-image outputs against award-winning posters and design works.
items.why: It tests whether generators produce good design when briefs leave appearance open, a gap beyond alignment and preference scores.

items.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
items.summary: A short paper argues that social robots still suffer from turn-taking failures and misunderstandings, and proposes multimodal bidirectional streaming to reduce them.
items.why: Turn-taking and misunderstanding remain practical barriers for spoken interfaces, even as speech recognition has improved.

items.title: Where in the Input Does a One-Pass Decision Encoder Look?
items.summary: Researchers study Laya, a small one-pass multiple-choice model, measuring how performance degrades when evidence sits later in a 512-token window.
items.why: It quantifies the cost of silent truncation for long documents in small models with fixed context windows.

items.title: PISim: A Unified Photonic Inference Simulator for Hardware-Aware Cross-Layer Design-Space Exploration
items.summary: PISim is a unified photonic inference simulator for cross-layer design-space exploration of photonic neural accelerators, covering electro-optical interfaces and physical non-idealities.
items.why: Hardware teams can evaluate photonic accelerator designs against neural workloads before fabrication, reducing costly iteration.

items.title: RESYNC: Residual Latent-State Synchronization for Deadline-Bound Streaming Inference
items.summary: RESYNC runs a large model asynchronously while a fast path updates its stale latent state, aiming to meet deadlines in high-rate streaming inference.
items.why: It offers a way to keep predictions fresh on streams where a large model would otherwise miss arrival deadlines.

items.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
items.summary: Researchers propose an agent-aided system in which a ground-control agent combines an LLM with an optimizer to schedule multiple drones in victim search missions.
items.why: It shows an LLM agent coordinating an optimization layer for real-time scheduling under uncertainty.

items.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
items.summary: Zyphra released ZONOS3-Mini, an 886M-parameter zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model with a new audio codec, claiming real-time operation on laptops and smartphones.
items.why: A compact, on-device voice-cloning model with reported multilingual accuracy lowers the bar for local speech applications.

items.title: When Chekhov's Gun Fires Anyway: Over-Realization in Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: Researchers define over-realization, where text-to-image models render prompted targets in contexts the prompt rules out, and introduce the OverReal benchmark.
items.why: Standard alignment metrics miss this failure, so teams relying on them may ship image generators that violate negations or beliefs.

items.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
items.summary: A new dataset distillation method learns synthetic samples that directly approximate per-class data distributions rather than optimizing for a classifier.
items.why: Distilled datasets that match data distributions could make training on small synthetic sets more reusable across downstream tasks.

items.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
items.summary: Researchers present coordinated optimizations that reduce batch makespan for LLM agent workloads, including GPU memory allocation between KV cache and recurrent state for hybrid models.
items.why: Batch agent evaluation and RL rollouts are costly; inference and environment coordination can cut completion time and GPU spend.

items.title: MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses
items.summary: MuSeToM is a human-validated text benchmark testing whether LLMs can judge if perceptual evidence justifies another person's belief revision across six senses.
items.why: It probes a social reasoning gap beyond static false-belief tests, relevant to agents reasoning about others' knowledge.

items.title: Edge-Gradient Augmentation under Reinforcement Learning for Temporal Graph
items.summary: EG-RL is a reinforcement learning framework for temporal link prediction that explicitly encodes edge births and deaths as edge-gradient events.
items.why: Explicit edge-change signals may improve link prediction in evolving graphs used for recommendation and social analysis.

items.title: MobileProbe: Adaptive Security Evaluation of Mobile Agents via Trajectory-Aware Injection
items.summary: MobileProbe is an adaptive security evaluation for mobile GUI agents that injects malicious instructions into screen content along agent trajectories, targeting environmental injection attacks.
items.why: Mobile agents act on whatever the screen shows, so injection-resistance testing matters for anyone shipping agent automation.

items.title: MusicRWKV: A Multimodal RWKV Framework for Music Representation Learning
items.summary: MusicRWKV is a multimodal music representation framework built on RWKV that jointly models waveform, spectrogram, and metadata with self-supervised learning.
items.why: RWKV's linear-complexity design offers an alternative to quadratic attention for long music recordings.

items.title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
items.summary: The paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture, a conceptual framework treating data, information, knowledge, understanding and wisdom as interacting epistemic functions.

items.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach
items.summary: A pilot study finds off-the-shelf general vision-language models adapt well to diverse driving tasks, with metric depth as the main gap, and introduces a Triplet Incremental Training approach.
items.why: It suggests driving VLMs may not need heavy 3D priors or architectural overhauls, with depth sensors or depth models closing the main gap.

items.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
items.summary: EgoX is a framework for learning manipulation policies from combined human, real robot, and simulated demonstrations using a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming.
items.why: It offers a way to pool heterogeneous demonstration data across morphologies and sensors, which could reduce data collection costs for robot policies.

items.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
items.summary: PhysLoop is a harness that uses LLM physics knowledge to guide self-improving video generation models toward more physically consistent training videos.
items.why: It proposes a way to generate physics-aware training data for video models without costly manual supervision, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: ORCA:Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment for Multi-View Clustering
items.summary: ORCA is a deep multi-view clustering method that uses orthogonal residual fusion and consensus-calibrated contrastive alignment to reduce redundancy and improve alignment.

items.title: AgriSense: Vision-Language Decision Support and Robotic Intervention in a Virtual Greenhouse Copy title
items.summary: AgriSense combines an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, and vision-language decision support for autonomous greenhouse management.
items.why: It shows an integrated simulation-to-robot pipeline pairing frozen encoders with environmental inputs for agricultural decisions, though the text gives few performance details.

items.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: A new benchmark evaluates Video LLMs on rare, safety-critical autonomous driving corner cases rather than routine traffic scenes.
items.why: Routine-scene benchmarks overstate readiness; teams deploying video LLMs in driving need tests focused on rare, safety-critical events.

items.title: DPA: Decentralized Primal Averaging with Quasi-Global Momentum for Highly Heterogeneous Data
items.summary: DPA is a decentralized learning algorithm combining primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer to handle highly heterogeneous data on sparse communication graphs.
items.why: It targets accuracy loss in decentralized training on heterogeneous, on-device data, a practical constraint for federated-style deployments.

items.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
items.summary: The Context Graph is a heterogeneous directed graph proposed to trace cross-agent decision chains among xApps and rApps in AI-RAN networks.
items.why: Operators of multi-agent radio networks need traceable decision chains to diagnose which agent caused a degradation.

items.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
items.summary: A diagnostic study shows protein language models' contact predictions fail to hold under a bijective relabeling of amino-acid letters, questioning that they learn invariant coevolutionary statistics.
items.why: It challenges the assumption that high accuracy from protein language models reflects robust underlying biological signal.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Verification in Dafny
items.summary: A paper presents a system that uses LLMs to assist with formal verification in Dafny, covering specifications, invariants, proofs, and solver diagnosis.
items.why: LLM-assisted formal verification could lower the expertise barrier for machine-checked correctness, though reliability remains a stated challenge.

items.title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search
items.summary: A codebook-based multi-bit watermarking scheme embeds payloads into LLM text via logit biasing and recovers them by nearest-codeword search.
items.why: It aims to attribute short LLM outputs to sources without long generations, relevant to provenance and misuse tracking.

items.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
items.summary: STEALTH shows provably secure linguistic steganography schemes often fail to decode when receiver precision, quantization, or GPU hardware differs from the sender's.
items.why: Engineers relying on bit-exact probability recomputation across hardware should expect steganographic and watermark decoding to break under numerical differences.

items.title: SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection
items.summary: SPADE introduces soft prompts to detect AI-generated text by modeling the generation process, rather than relying only on the text or its probabilities.
items.why: Detectors that account for prompts may be more robust in open-world settings, though the text gives little on benchmark results.

items.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
items.summary: Kezek splits mono recordings of two-person conversations into separate per-speaker tracks, preserving timing and overlaps, to create full-duplex dialogue training data.
items.why: It offers a way to turn abundant single-channel conversation audio into training data for full-duplex spoken dialogue models.

items.title: Why You Should Expect an AI Crash
items.summary: The Economist's leader argues that an AI crash should be expected, according to a Hacker News post linking to the article.

items.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
items.summary: Edge0 has introduced Edge0-145B, a model it says offers frontier AI capabilities that run on a user's own computer.

items.title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
items.summary: Democrats launched a Congressional investigation into Nvidia's China sales and its dealings with Trump, the second such probe since an alleged spy affair surfaced.
items.why: Heightened congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China sales could bring new export-control or compliance pressure on the chip supply chain.

items.title: Muse can now place calls to US businesses — if you pay
items.summary: Muse's AI can now place outbound calls to U.S. businesses, but the feature requires a paid plan.

items.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
items.summary: AWS made SGLang-Neuron publicly available through a Deep Learning Container for serving models and generating RL rollouts on Trainium.
items.why: Teams on AWS Trainium can serve models and run RL rollouts with the familiar SGLang interface on native PyTorch.

items.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
items.summary: A forensic analysis claims Chinese frontier AI models carry traces of export-controlled GPUs, per a post with 139 Hacker News points.
items.why: If accurate, it suggests export-controlled hardware is embedded in models, relevant to compliance and provenance decisions.

items.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Natera built SWARM, an agentic lab-operations system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, reporting about 130x faster first response and 96.2% automated support-ticket coverage.
items.why: It offers a concrete architecture and reported results for deploying agentic AI on institutional knowledge in enterprise support workflows.

items.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
items.summary: Nebius plans to fund a $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, amid delays at a Microsoft data center.
items.why: Neocloud financing that relies on customer prepayments and loans raises questions about capacity delivery and vendor risk for cloud buyers.

items.title: AI is turning Apple's app review process into a nightmare for synth developers
items.summary: A synth developer post says AI is complicating Apple's app review process, creating difficulties for synthesizer app developers.

items.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost
items.summary: AWS explains four request-level Amazon Bedrock settings (cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, maxTokens) that change token processing and billing, with testing results.
items.why: Engineers can cut Bedrock inference costs by tuning these request settings and verifying their effect on token usage.

items.title: Jensen Huang was having a third affair, Reuters reports
items.summary: Reuters reports Jensen Huang had a third affair, this time with an unnamed Nvidia employee, which Reuters says it is withholding by name.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.summary: Nvidia reportedly told Rep. Bill Foster that tracking chips to fight smuggling is technically possible, though an industry group called the measures potentially infeasible.
items.why: Feasibility of chip-tracking under the Chip Security Act affects hardware compliance requirements and supply chain obligations.

items.title: How Amplitude ships product improvements in 1–2 days with OpenAI
items.summary: Amplitude describes how it ships product improvements in one to two days using OpenAI models, with its Wave product agent and coding agents.
items.why: It shows a production pattern of pairing a product agent with coding agents to shorten release cycles.

items.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
items.summary: AWS describes using IAM principal tags, CUR 2.0 or Cost Explorer, and AWS Budgets actions to track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per identity.
items.why: Engineering leaders can enforce per-identity Bedrock spend limits with AWS-native tooling, often without application code changes.

items.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions
items.summary: Google says its AI Mode in Search now better handles complex queries, surfaces relevant links, and gives richer visual responses, powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen.
items.why: Signals Google's Search model upgrades, which may shape how users find and consume information and how publishers get traffic.

items.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands
items.summary: Nectar launched an AI agent that automates influencer marketing, including creator discovery, outreach, partnership management, and campaign result tracking.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.summary: LLMON, an LLM-native markup language, is now available in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B models, according to Hugging Face.

items.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: AWS outlines how to calculate true per-task cost on Amazon Bedrock, reduce it with caching, routing and output limits, and measure agent ROI.
items.why: Per-token prices understate real costs, so teams need per-task cost and ROI measurement to justify running agents in production.

items.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
items.summary: AWS shows how to build a self-service LLM gateway using LiteLLM on Fargate that exposes Bedrock models via an OpenAI-compatible API with per-user controls.
items.why: Platform teams can offer developers instant model access while keeping per-user cost controls, quota isolation, and observability.

items.summary: An opinion piece criticizes Palantir CEO Alex Karp's recent political repositioning and comments on last week's elections.

items.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Google announced a major Google Search upgrade powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen, shown through a card carousel with product examples.

items.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime
items.summary: AWS announced the next-generation Bedrock AgentCore runtime, offering hardware-isolated sessions, faster starts, more compute, usage-based billing, and data isolation.
items.why: Long-running agents need isolated, scalable compute, and this runtime targets secure multi-hour agent workloads with usage-based pricing.

items.title: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
items.summary: SoftBank lost over $3 billion on preordered natural gas turbines intended to power AI data centers, and the article examines the impact on power markets.
items.why: Shows financial risk in securing power infrastructure for AI data centers, which can constrain energy-intensive AI buildouts.

items.title: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots
items.summary: Phota Labs is building AI that automates photo editing to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots for consumers.

items.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
items.summary: A study by IP protection firm Podqi found AI chatbots including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity can recommend fake retail websites to shoppers.
items.why: Shows that AI assistant shopping recommendations carry phishing and impersonation risk that product teams need to account for.

items.title: More game developers are starting to use generative AI
items.summary: A GDC survey found 40% of game developers use generative AI as part of their job, up from 36% in 2025.
items.why: Gives a benchmark for generative AI adoption among professional game developers year over year.

items.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
items.summary: An article argues that Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang used his influence to push the AI industry in specific ways, and that his departure could affect it.

items.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent
items.summary: AWS describes how a coding agent using the amazon-bedrock skill can migrate a customer-managed Bedrock knowledge base to a Managed Knowledge Base with read-only discovery and validation.
items.why: Gives teams a guided, validated path to move RAG knowledge bases to managed infrastructure without disrupting retrieval.

items.title: Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS
items.summary: AWS shows how to build a multi-agent system where a LangChain orchestrator on ECS talks to a Strands agent on Bedrock AgentCore via the A2A protocol.
items.why: It demonstrates cross-framework, cross-organization agent interoperability with OAuth-authenticated, bidirectional calls, without shared SDK dependencies.

items.title: Fine-grained access control for Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base tools
items.summary: AWS explains exposing a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base to agents as MCP tools via AgentCore Gateway while enforcing per-user access control.
items.why: It offers a pattern for securing agent access to enterprise knowledge bases using verified identity injection, independent policy checks, and resource-based restrictions.

items.title: From prototype to production: Engineering agents with Agent DLC
items.summary: AWS introduces Agent DLC, a lifecycle framework for measuring agent quality and checking whether each change helps, addressing gaps in traditional CI/CD.
items.why: Aggregate metrics can hide coverage gaps, so teams moving agents to production need repeatable evaluation loops for every change.

items.title: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund
items.summary: Norwest has raised a $4 billion fund, its largest to date, to deepen its AI investing.

items.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers’ chat transcripts
items.summary: A cyberattack on Fireworks AI let hackers access Notion customers' chat transcripts, marking Fireworks' second data breach in two months.
items.why: Repeated breaches at an AI infrastructure vendor highlight the need to vet third-party AI providers and limit sensitive data exposure.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after acknowledging an affair, and The New York Times reported evidence of another affair with a direct report.
items.why: Leadership turmoil at Nvidia, the leading AI chip supplier, could affect company direction and partner confidence.

items.title: I reviewed the Apple HomeView, ask me anything
items.summary: The Verge's smart home reviewer tested Apple's first smart display, the $299 HomeView, in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, and opened the review to reader questions.

items.title: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW
items.summary: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV arrives on GeForce NOW, with DLSS 5 coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet.

items.title: Nine Korean startups vie for a spot in Disrupt 2027’s Startup Battlefield 200 competition
items.summary: Nine Korean startups are competing for a spot in Disrupt 2027's Startup Battlefield 200, spanning deep tech sectors including AI, healthcare, and semiconductors.

items.title: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex
items.summary: Gondola says it doubled revenue and that Codex raised its lead engineer's output by 50%, alongside ChatGPT simplifying daily work.

items.summary: Holiday Extras is using OpenAI's Codex to turn customer expertise into better apps, higher booking conversion, and new growth opportunities.

items.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors
items.summary: TechCrunch published a speculative shortlist of possible successors to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, noting the company has no succession plan.

items.title: Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI
items.summary: AWS shows Java developers how to build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI, covering tool calling, memory, resilience, multi-agent orchestration, and deployment to AgentCore.
items.why: Gives Java teams a concrete production pattern for agents on AWS, spanning tool calling, memory, resilience, and deployment.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary: OpenAI published a conversation with Sam Nickless, CEO of Gilbert + Tobin, about rethinking the law firm business with AI.
items.why: Shows how a large professional services firm is restructuring its operations around AI, a useful case study for enterprise adoption leaders.

items.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
items.summary: OpenAI committed $2 million to research on AI and children's safety, supporting shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.
items.why: Signals growing investment in standardized measurement of AI risks for minors, which may shape future safety evaluation practices.

items.title: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
items.summary: Hugging Face published a definitive fine-tuning guide for 3D generation models.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: TechCrunch publishes a timeline of an affair scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which it says could affect national security amid US-China AI infrastructure competition.

items.title: OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: AWS publishes a guide for enterprises rolling out OpenAI Codex to developers, using Amazon Bedrock as the model backend and covering access, governance, and cost decisions.
items.why: Outlines the access, governance, and cost decisions platform, security, and finance teams must align on before a Codex rollout.

items.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification
items.summary: AWS describes computing a deterministic semantic diff of formal authorization policies using an open-source anti-unification engine, so reviewers see only behavior-changing differences.
items.why: Helps teams review authorization policy changes by surfacing behavioral differences rather than cosmetic text edits.

items.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
items.summary: AWS explains how to detect silent GPU data corruption in PyTorch DDP training, localize the faulty node on SageMaker HyperPod, and trigger automatic node replacement.
items.why: Gives ML infrastructure teams a way to catch silent GPU errors that could quietly corrupt distributed training runs.

items.title: Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: AWS launches a Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that lets code search the web via a single signed API call, with no gateway or resources to create.
items.why: Lets developers add web search to agents and pipelines through the AWS SDK or CLI without provisioning extra resources.

items.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
items.summary: The Verge reports, citing WSJ and NYT, that Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang after a second alleged extramarital affair was reported.

items.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026
items.summary: AWS publishes a recap of October 2026 updates to Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, including new models, agent availability features, and clearer cost reporting.
items.why: Summarizes recent platform changes that affect agent availability, grounding, and cost tracking on AWS.

items.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
items.summary: United Airlines has reportedly banned AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers, according to a CBS News report shared on Hacker News.
items.why: Signals that some large travel providers are restricting third-party AI agents, which affects agent-driven booking designs.

items.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track
items.summary: AWS published an attendee guide to the AI/ML track at re:Invent 2026, which includes more than 140 sessions.
items.why: It helps engineers pick sessions on AI chips, inference, agents, and agent trust for their role and goals.

items.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
items.summary: AWS shows how to automatically update the AWS Agent Registry using an event-driven pipeline that detects MCP server changes.
items.why: Teams running agents across accounts can keep tool metadata current without storing secrets.

items.title: How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: DXC Technology describes DCX OASIS, its Human+AI operating model built on a multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock.
items.why: It shows a pattern for separating the model layer from a governance harness that orchestrates and audits agents at scale.

items.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
items.summary: Many announced data center projects may never be built, adding to local opposition, permitting delays, and electricity shortages.
items.why: Infrastructure planners should expect capacity announcements to slip, making delivery timelines less reliable.

items.title: Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
items.summary: Meta's longtime head of infrastructure, Santosh Janardhan, is stepping down from the role.
items.why: Leadership changes in Meta's infrastructure organization could affect the direction of its large-scale systems.

items.title: How backlash and red tape continue to slow data centers post-Blue Wave
items.summary: Local backlash, permitting delays, and electricity constraints are slowing data center projects, and many announced projects may never be built.
items.why: Engineering leaders relying on planned capacity should account for delays and cancellations in their roadmaps.

items.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
items.summary: CoreWeave is asking customers for upfront payments and offering shorter contracts, according to its third-quarter earnings.
items.why: Shifts in GPU cloud contract terms affect cost planning and capacity commitments for AI teams.

items.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
items.summary: Britain's Fractile raised a $720M round, making it one of the top-funded startups building purpose-built AI chips.
items.why: Well-funded alternatives to GPUs could broaden the hardware options for AI inference and training.

items.title: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair
items.summary: House Republicans have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for a closed-door briefing about his alleged affair with a Chinese spy.
items.why: Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's leadership could carry implications for the company and its chip supply.

items.title: Accelerating generative AI delivery with reusable assets
items.summary: AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center offers a catalog of 23 open source, production-ready reusable assets for generative AI delivery.
items.why: Teams can reuse tested RAG pipelines, document processors, and agent scaffolding instead of rebuilding them.

items.title: Retirement Savings Are Fueling the AI Bubble
items.summary: A blog post argues that retirement savings are fueling the AI bubble, linking pension and retirement investment to AI market valuations.

items.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
items.summary: Google announced the Gemini Decisions API, powered by its Gemini Decision model, for fast, calibrated multimodal decisions.

items.title: AI, activity, and outcomes in software engineering
items.summary: A linked video discusses AI's effects on activity and outcomes in software engineering, shared on Hacker News with no further detail in the feed.

items.title: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems?
items.summary: An investment intel consultant says many senior industry figures know about Jensen Huang's alleged misconduct and effectively condone it.
items.why: Reputational and governance concerns around Nvidia's leadership may matter to investors and partners.

items.title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time
items.summary: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crossed $10 billion for the first time, up almost 50% from $6.7 billion in the prior second quarter.
items.why: Rapid revenue growth at a leading model provider signals sustained enterprise and consumer demand for AI services.

items.title: Accelerating product development with AI-driven lifecycle management (AI-PDLC) in AWS Quick
items.summary: AWS describes an AI-driven product development lifecycle using six AWS Quick agents, with human approval at each gate and handoff to coding agents like Kiro.
items.why: It offers a structured workflow for turning customer signals into prototypes and specs for coding agents.

items.title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
items.summary: Google Labs released Tabletop, a experimental collaborative space for building itineraries, polls, and brackets, with a waitlist.

items.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents
items.summary: AWS ML Blog describes UAEF, a framework-agnostic system that converts agent traces into one canonical format and scores them with 36 metrics across 7 dimensions.
items.why: Teams running agents across multiple frameworks can compare versions and catch regressions with one shared evaluation pipeline.

items.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming
items.summary: AWS Marketplace now supports usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming inference, with Deepgram as launch partner for speech-to-text and text-to-speech.
items.why: Engineers building live voice or streaming AI services can now bill customers per consumed usage through AWS Marketplace.

items.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
items.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a successor model that aims to explain how DNA changes affect different cells and the causes of disease.

items.title: Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth
items.summary: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says he uses the revised Genie agent to surface problems his 12,000 employees are unlikely to report directly.

items.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads
items.summary: Plurai is working on improving AI agents by applying an end-to-end training approach similar to the one used for self-driving cars.
items.why: Engineers building agents may find the idea of training for probabilistic, unpredictable environments relevant, though the text gives few details.

items.title: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
items.summary: Adobe announced experimental AI features at its Max conference, including turning images into explorable 3D scenes, designing AI characters through conversation, and copy/paste-style photo editing.

items.title: Google SWE points 48 AI agents at NASA Lidar, finds unmapped Maya pyramid in 72h
items.summary: A Hacker News post describes Google SWE using 48 AI agents on NASA Lidar data that reportedly found an unmapped Maya pyramid in 72 hours.
items.why: It shows multi-agent systems applied to large geospatial datasets, though the description gives little detail on the method.
